subjects.displayTitle: Divine oneness: beyond number, likeness, and possession
subjects.introduction: To say that God is one is not to count. Bahá’u’lláh prays to the One who is single in no numerical sense, and the Báb strips the Divine Essence of every likeness, partner and similitude, so that oneness means freedom from comparison rather than the first step in a series. Yet the same Writings overflow with intimacy: lovers perplexed by a mystery they cannot fathom, atoms and hairs bearing witness, a lamp and a leaf confessing what no mind can hold. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá offers the sun that shines in many mirrors without ever descending into them, and Bahá’u’lláh the painter whose work points to him without becoming him; both images guard nearness and transcendence at once. The terms ahadiyyih and wahidiyyih open onto the names and attributes of God, the subtle cloud that is seen and unseen, and the eternal archetypes, while the question of idolatry asks what thought may mistake for its Maker. The Shema’s call to love the one God wholeheartedly and to speak of him at home and on the road [1] turns confession into a rhythm of living, and that is finally what oneness asks: that a life, and a gathering of lives, become its sign.
subjects.arc: Begin with the limits of number and the distinction between maker and sign; explore essence, names and manifestation; pass through devotional testimony and the witness of creation; return to human unity before comparing the supplied philosophical voices.

order.why: Enter the extended explanation through the dot, numbers, and the Hidden Treasure.
shortened: For example, consider the dot (or point); how letters and words are folded up and hidden within the essence (huwiyyat , ipseity) and reality of a dot with perfect effacement and annihilation so that no trace can be discerned of the existence of these letters and words nor is there any differentiation between them.  Rather they are completely obliterated and utterly annihilated and have no existence except in the essence (dhat) of the point.  In the same way the Names and Attributes of God and the Essential Dispositions [shu'unat dhatiyya]  are completely and utterly annihilated in the station of Primary Oneness so that not a whiff can be inhaled from them of substantial or intellectual existence.   This original point is the "Hidden Treasure" of these letters and words and they were incorporated and immersed within it and from it they appeared.

And similarly consider the Unitary Concept [ahad]; how all the numbers appear from it and it is in no number since it is the point of origin of all numbers.  And the first to be specified and to appear from it is the number "one" [wahid] and from "one" all other numbers come into being.  So all these numbers are contained in the unitary concept in the most perfect simplicity and oneness.  And so it is the "Hidden Treasure" of all numbers and from it do they appear.

order.why: Open with the surprising refusal to make divine oneness an ordinary number.
Give the question a tangible image through painter and painting.
shortened: Consider the relation between the craftsman and his handiwork, between the painter and his painting.

Can it ever be maintained that the work their hands have produced is the same as themselves? By Him Who is the Lord of the Throne above and of earth below! They can be regarded in no other light except as evidences that proclaim the excellence and perfection of their author.

order.why: Explore the many mirrors and one sun without collapsing their distinction.
shortened: Although it transcends our realization, its lights, bestowals, traces and virtues have become manifest in the realities of the Prophets, even as the sun becomes resplendent in various mirrors. These holy realities are as reflectors, and the reality of Divinity is as the sun, which, although it is reflected from the mirrors, and its virtues and perfections become resplendent therein, does not stoop from its own station of majesty and glory and seek abode in the mirrors; it remains in its heaven of sanctity. At most it is this: that its lights become manifest and evident in its mirrors or manifestations. Therefore, its bounty proceeding from them is one bounty, but the recipients of that bounty are many. This is the unity of God; this is oneness -- unity of Divinity, holy above ascent or descent, embodiment, comprehension or idealization -- divine unity.

order.why: Admit the difficulty of comprehension in the reported reflection.
Let confessed powerlessness become a beginning of understanding.
shortened: From eternity Thou hast, in Thy transcendent oneness, been immeasurably exalted above Thy servants' conception of Thy unity, and wilt to eternity remain, in Thine unapproachable singleness, far above the praise of Thy creatures. No words that any one beside Thee may utter can ever beseem Thee, and no man's description except Thine own description can befit Thy nature. All who adore Thy unity have been sore perplexed to fathom the mystery of Thy oneness, and all have confessed their powerlessness to attain unto the comprehension of Thine essence and to scale the pinnacle of Thy knowledge.

order.why: State the insistence on freedom from likeness.
shortened: True belief in the unity of God [tawhid-i-haqiqi] consists in acknowledging and confessing the unity of God, exalted be His glory, sanctifying His Essence from all likeness and purifying His Being from all similitudes. This has ever been and shall ever be the case.

order.why: Connect that oneness with certitude and detachment.
Hear the simple repeated denial of peers and equals.
shortened: Thou art One, no partner hast Thou; Thou art One, no peer hast Thou; Thou art One, no equal hast Thou; Thou art One, no likeness hast Thou! Thou art unique in Thy oneness and sanctified in Thy singleness.

order.why: Read the compact declaration of oneness and incomparability.
shortened: Say:
He is God, the One! God, the Eternal! He begetteth not, nor was begotten, and there is none comparable unto Him.

order.why: Keep the letter’s historical attribution concerning Abraham in its own setting.
Introduce the distinction of unity in the Divine Essence.
Read the Bab’s account of names, essence and the relation to creation.
shortened: His Essence hath no attribute or name besides His Essence. He is the Truth, there is no God but Him. Thee do we worship and Thine aid we seek.
All else besides Him are brought into being through His creation and origination. There is neither connection nor separation between Him and contingent beings.

order.why: Consider knowledge that does not depend on the prior existence of its objects.
shortened: He knoweth all things as they are, whether universals or particulars, substances or accidents, after their creation just as on the day He had not created them. He knoweth them because knowledge is life, and just as God, glory be to Him, is Ever-Living in the eternity of eternities, and needeth not the existence of any living thing to prove His life, He was All-Knowing of all things without there being any object of knowledge.

order.why: Compare the distinctions among essence, necessity and contingency.
shortened: For existence is either identical with quiddity or other than it. If other than it, is it inseparable from it and among its requirements without suspension or detachment, or is suspension and detachment possible?

The first is the reality of the Essence from the perspective of its oneness - its existence is identical with its quiddity and its quiddity identical with its existence. The second is the station of necessity, where existence is distinct from quiddity but inseparable from it in a way that neither detachment nor separation can be conceived, for it is among its requirements. The third is the station of contingency - that is, existence derived from another and acquired from what is other than itself. Here its existence is other than its quiddity and its quiddity other than its existence, with the possibility of detachment and separation.

order.why: Use the subtle cloud to explore specification that is seen and unseen.
shortened: Al-'Ama' in the language means a very light and subtle cloud that is seen and unseen. If you gaze with utmost care you find something, but as soon as you look, it cannot be seen. That is why, in the tradition of the investigators, by Al-'Ama' they mean the Universal Reality with no specifications, for specifications exist in the mode of simplicity and unity and are not distinguished from the essence. So it is both specified and unspecified, and this station is described as Divine Oneness and Al-'Ama', and it is the station of the Hidden Treasure mentioned in the Hadith.

order.why: Keep the concise explanation concerning universal meanings.
Read the movement from unity toward oneness as an invitation to effort.
shortened: Therefore strive and sacrifice yourself, make every effort despite distress, so that your speaking reality and your eternal archetype may turn from the station of unity toward the heart-expanding wilderness of oneness.

order.why: Retain the numerical and talismanic imagery in the letter’s own register.
Explore the cited tradition concerning the hidden and manifested Name.
shortened: Again, in al-Kafi, from Abu 'Abdu'llah -- peace be upon him -- He said: Verily God, blessed and exalted, created a Name -- of letters, yet unvocalized; of utterance, yet unpronounced; of person, yet unembodied; by likeness, yet undescribed; of colour, yet untinged. Denied of it are the confines of direction; far removed from the senses of all who sense -- hidden, yet not concealed. He made it a steadfast Word upon four parts together -- none preceding another. Of these He manifested three as a Name, by reason of the creatures' need for them, and He veiled one thereof -- and that is the Hidden, Treasured Name.

order.why: Let the description of Hahut mark a limit to interpretation.
shortened: Among them is the station of the Throne of Hahut, the Paradise of Oneness. None can interpret a single letter of that verse in that Paradise, for this is the station of the mystery of the Divine Eternality, the edifices of Unity, the Israel of Singleness, and the essence of Luminosity. Its outward is identical with its inward, and its inward identical with its outward. It behooveth no one to comprehend a single letter thereof, but God shall reveal it, when He willeth, to whom He willeth.

order.why: Distinguish glorification from a claim to attain the Divine Essence.
shortened: God hath desired naught from the expression of unity save the word of glorification, and from it naught save the word of praise, and from it naught save the word of His oneness, and from it naught save the word of His greatness. For the unity of the Divine Essence, as established in the beginning and end of the Command, is impossible for any created thing to attain, nor can any claim "I am capable of this," for such a statement would be pure falsehood and manifest untruth, and can only operate within its own rank.

order.why: Examine what the pronouns He and Thou can and cannot indicate.
Keep the separate reflection on the limits of the expression He is He.
Follow the related expression through the face of revelation.
Read the startling Thou art I in its devotional source context.
Distinguish a name’s ordinary reference from its relation to the Truth.
shortened: O seeker! Though a name indicates that which is named, this applies only to the realm of creation. But the Truth is sanctified above all names - all names end in His Most Exalted Word and all attributes return to His Primal Will. Whoever attains unto Him has attained unto all names, both now and forever.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s critique of Simple Reality and the Trinity contextually attributed.
Read creation through the Will alongside the assertion of transcendence.
Retain the source’s distinction from everything created or to be created.
Consider the failure of names and attributes before enduring oneness.
shortened: There is no God but Thee! Thou hast ever been as Thou wert. Attributes have gone astray, names have been cut off, and traces have returned. And now Thou art as Thou hast ever been in might and oneness.

order.why: Join unity of essence and attributes with transcendence of praise.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one in Thy Essence and one in Thy attributes, sanctified above every wondrous mention and every beauteous praise, and Thou wilt ever continue to be what Thou hast been from time immemorial.

order.why: Discusses unity of essence, attributes, deeds and worship.
Keep the concise separate statement on essence and attributes.
shortened: The Wronged One testifies that there is none other God but Him. He has ever been One in His Essence and One in His attributes.

order.why: Read unity in dominion alongside unity in essence.
Preserve the brief independent affirmation of incomparability.
shortened: He hath ever been One in His Essence, having taken neither partner nor peer unto Himself.

order.why: Extend the statement to actions and sufficiency.
shortened: Find sufficiency in Him rather than in aught else, and associate not any partner with Him, for verily He is One in His essence and then in His actions, were ye of them that know.

order.why: Ask how a coequal would contradict incomparability.
shortened: From everlasting Thou wert alone, with none to describe Thee, and wilt abide for ever the same with no one else to equal or rival Thee. Were the existence of any co-equal with Thee to be recognized, how could it then be maintained that Thou art the Incomparable, or that Thy Godhead is immeasurably exalted above all peers or likeness?

order.why: Hear the extended exclusion of rival, opposite and likeness.
shortened: And thy Lord hath taken unto Himself no partner, nor any peer, nor any minister, nor any likeness, nor any equal, nor any opposite, nor any similitude.

order.why: Keep the warning against associating partners.
shortened: Beware lest thou ascribe partners unto Him Who hath ever been One in His Essence and hath taken neither peer nor likeness unto Himself. To this beareth witness all that hath been sent down aforetime from the presence of the Mighty, the Bestower.

order.why: Preserve the separate warning and invitation to testimony.
Read the absence of likeness as integral to recognition.
shortened: And this recognition is not complete except through acknowledging His oneness and confessing His singleness, in such wise that no likeness, peer, similitude or equal be seen for Him.

order.why: Keep the concise reference to sanctification from peers.
Consider the testimony of creation alongside the inadequacy of all description.
shortened: He hath ever existed, sanctified from all peers and likenesses, and exalted above all that hath been said or shall be said. He hath been, and is, the One, the Single, the Unique, the Self-Subsisting, the Eternal--He unto Whose oneness and singleness the tongues of all created things have testified, and through Whose remembrance and praise all things have spoken.

order.why: Introduce divine self-testimony independent of any creature.
shortened: God testifieth to the unity of His Godhood and to the singleness of His own Being. On the throne of eternity, from the inaccessible heights of His station, His tongue proclaimeth that there is none other God but Him. He Himself, independently of all else, hath ever been a witness unto His own oneness, the revealer of His own nature, the glorifier of His own essence.

order.why: Distinguish self-revelation from manifestation through signs.
Invite inward acknowledgment of the testimony.
shortened: Bear thou witness in thine inmost heart unto this testimony which God hath Himself and for Himself pronounced, that there is none other God but Him, that all else besides Him have been created by His behest, have been fashioned by His leave, are subject to His law, are as a thing forgotten when compared to the glorious evidences of His oneness, and are as nothing when brought face to face with the mighty revelations of His unity.

order.why: Read the Bab’s account of knowledge through the Prophet.
Explore how a Manifestation’s oneness demonstrates divine unity.
shortened: Thy unity is inscrutable, O my God, to all except them that have recognized Him Who is the Manifestation of Thy singleness and the Day-Spring of Thy oneness. Whoso assigneth a rival unto Him hath assigned a rival unto Thee, and whoso hath set up a peer for Him hath set up a peer for Thyself. No, no, none can withstand Thee in the whole of creation. Thou hast everlastingly been exalted far above all comparison and likeness. Thy oneness hath been demonstrated by the oneness of Him Who is the Dawning-Place of Thy Revelation.

order.why: Read the first-person proclamation of creation through Will and Purpose.
shortened: And God addresseth therein all who are in the heavens and on earth, and all that hath been and shall be, saying: "There is no God but Me, Who created all contingent things from nothing through My Will, and brought all beings into existence from naught through My Purpose. I am the One with power over whatsoever I desire, and I am the All-Encompassing, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Consider Messengers and Books as dawning-places of names and attributes.
Connect recognition with teaching the path of oneness.
shortened: I testify that Thou didst create me for the recognition of the Dayspring of Thy Revelation and the Dawning-place of Thy signs and the Manifestation of Thy Self, and Thou hast revealed unto Thy servants that which draweth them nigh unto the court of Thy glory, and taught them the oneness of Thy Being and Thy sanctification from all peers and likenesses, and made them to know Thy straight path and Thy firm and mighty command.

order.why: Preserve the source’s account of true recognition and the absence of number.
Read the renewed decree and Nightingale’s testimony.
shortened: Say: Through this Revelation the decree of origination is established and the Nightingale of the All-Merciful hath sung upon the branches of the Tree of Utterance that "There is none other God beside Me, the Single, the All-Informed." Say: Whosoever affirmeth a likeness hath indeed associated partners with God - to this doth the Ancient Beauty testify from His exalted station.

order.why: Keep the Tree’s utterance in its stated station.
shortened: And in another station it referreth to this Breast wherein the Tree uttereth: "There is none other God but Me, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."

order.why: Return to the one sun reflected according to capacity.
Read existence as a garment received through light.
Consider the enduring radiance of the divine Sun.
shortened: From the beginning that has no beginning, the lights of the glory of divine unity have shone forth without pause or delay, and the radiant gleams of the divine Sun have ever appeared and will continue to appear without concealment or diminution.

order.why: Bring the dawning of unity into the horizon of the soul.
Keep the image of a sun shining upon visible and unseen realms.
shortened: And therein did the Sun of Thy oneness shine forth from the horizon of the House upon all who dwell in the unseen and the visible realms.

order.why: Extend the proclamation of oneness across religions.
shortened: This is a day wherein grace hath encompassed all religions, and the Divine Lott Tree hath called out from the Most Exalted Horizon: 'Verily, there is none other God but Him, the One, the Single, the All-Knowing.'

order.why: Hear the call of the Leaf and Tree in its symbolic register.
Read the reflection on ordered creation and the Gate in its own source.
shortened: O people of the earth! Have you not reflected upon the creation of the heavens and the earth? If there were two gates in them from the Remembrance, they would have corrupted. And verily God has arranged the kingdom through His Gate of Truth, and God is indeed knowing of all things.

order.why: Attend to the testimony of seen and unseen existence.
shortened: O Lord! All things testify to Thy oneness, and whatsoever can be described as having existence, whether seen or unseen, beareth witness to Thy singleness.

order.why: Let the scale contract to atoms.
Keep the separate testimony of created things.
shortened: All created things have borne witness to Thy unity, and every dweller in Thy kingdom hath confessed Thy oneness.

order.why: Retain the parallel wording concerning all existing things.
shortened: All created things bear witness to Thy singleness, and all existing things to Thy oneness.

order.why: Read appearances and realities as signs.
shortened: All appearances and realities indicate the oneness of Thine Essence, and all evidences and signs reflect the truth that Thou art God and there is no peer or partner for Thee throughout the kingdoms of heaven and earth.

order.why: Keep the concise statement of universal testimony.
shortened: Thou art He to Whose oneness and singleness all have testified.

order.why: Give understanding and speech their own place in witness.
Hear the declaration through all things.
Let a lamp speak of illuminating creation.
Attend to the striking personification of hair.
Expand testimony through the whole body and its faculties.
Keep the distinct enumeration of tongue, heart, pen and hairs.
Join embodied witness with creation through the divine Word.
Read inward and outward testimony with the First and Last.
shortened: When you attain unto My Tablet and find the fragrance of your Lord's verses, say: "My God, my God! My outer and inner tongue, my limbs and members, my veins and the very hairs of my body bear witness to Your unity and oneness, and that You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.

order.why: Preserve the separately voiced bodily confession.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! My outward and inward tongue, my limbs and members all bear witness to Thy oneness and Thy singleness, and that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Single, the One, the Powerful, the All-Compelling, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Bring pen, tongue and inmost reality together.
Keep the paired inward and outward testimony to enduring oneness.
shortened: My outward and inward tongue both testify that Thou hast ever been One God, Single, Sole, Self-Subsisting, and wilt ever continue to be even as Thou hast been. There is no God but Thee, the Mighty, the Dominant, the Powerful, the Omnipotent.

order.why: Enter the Book of Names through its many forms of praise and sovereignty.
shortened: Praise be to God, Who hath exalted Himself in His transcendence above all contingent things, Who hath manifested His sovereignty above all created things, Who hath demonstrated His dominion above all things that have being, Who hath shown His might above all atoms, and Who hath revealed His grandeur above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven. He is the One beside Whom there is no equal, the Most Exalted above all likeness and duration, and the Most Holy, sanctified beyond every attribute and number. He hath created what He willeth by His command and ordained what He desireth by His sovereignty. Every created thing beareth witness that there is none other God but Him - a testimony purified from the ways of associating partners with God and from all veils, sanctified from the paths of remoteness and separation.

order.why: Read repeated confession alongside the degrees of names and attributes.
shortened: And in every night and day, say nineteen times "There is no God but God" in truth, in very truth, for even if thou shouldst say it unto infinity, there hath been and shall be but one Divine Unity, for in names there appeareth naught but the Named One Himself, even as thou sayest there is no sun but the true Sun, shouldst thou observe. Yet consider thou the degrees of unity in relation to the degrees of names and attributes, for in the presence of every true soul that which is contrary to it hath been and shall be negated, and unto God is the journey's end.

order.why: Follow the Book of Reckoning’s extended rhythm of return, praise and command.
shortened: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All stand before His presence. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All glorify Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All proclaim His oneness. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All magnify Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All extol His greatness.

order.why: Let the Book of Thirty Prayers carry oneness through every direction and condition.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Unique, Independent, Self-Subsisting, Self-Sufficient. Thou hast taken neither consort nor offspring, nor hath there been any partner with Thee, neither before nor after.

I testify to Thy independence of me and of all things, and I acknowledge Thy oneness before all things and after all things and above all things and beneath all things and to the right of all things and to the left of all things, that Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be free from the praise of any besides Thee and sanctified from that which Thy creation may acclaim.

order.why: Keep the ordinance of confession in the First Gate.
Read the repeated declaration and the passing of all save the divine countenance.
Join knowledge and choice with inseparable attributes.
Retain the independent prayer denying consort, son and helper.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, living, enduring, sovereign, all-pervading, holy, everlasting, forever, inaccessible, possessing, ruling, manifest, powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any helper in what Thou hast fashioned.

order.why: Hear the parallel devotional denial of likeness and generation.
Keep the distinct prayer’s sequence of divine qualities.
Read precise ordainment within the prayer for Ahmad.
Consider the formation of things through power and will.
shortened: Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, nor hath there been any partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned. Thou hast created all things by Thy power with precision, and formed all things by Thy will with perfection.

order.why: Keep the further refusal of limiting similitude.
shortened: Thou art He Who hath no equal, no peer, no likeness, no companion, no similitude, and Thou art He Who begetteth not, nor wast Thou begotten, Who cannot be limited or described by any similitude.

order.why: Connect perfect form with the submission of all realms.
shortened: Thou hast created all things by Thy power, in due measure, and hast fashioned the creation of all things by Thy will, with perfect form. Thou art He before Whom all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them prostrate themselves; and all who are in the realms of command and creation and whatsoever is beneath them are humble and submissive.

order.why: Preserve the separate prayer’s affirmation of enduring sovereignty.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, living, unchanging, sovereign, supreme, holy, everlasting, endless, inaccessible, exalted, ruling, possessing, glorified, powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned.

order.why: Keep the independent account of divine self-sufficiency.
Let the brief confession provide a pause.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, single, unique, ever-living, self-subsisting, eternal, everlasting.

order.why: Retain the distinct letter’s affirmation of holiness and justice.
Keep the concise instruction to praise.
Read the witness of creation in the memorial context of a Letter of the Living.
Preserve the separate memorial prayer for the second Letter.
shortened: Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Unique, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, the Ever-Abiding, the Ever-Enduring, the Self-Dependent. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast no partner in what Thou hast created, nor any protector in what Thou hast fashioned.

order.why: Keep the fifth Letter’s memorial invocation of inaccessible sovereignty.
Retain the supplied omission within the visitation for Quddus.
shortened: Then upon Thee, O Light of the Divine Identity, and Garment of the Countenance of Oneness, and Mystery of Eternality, and the Divine Grandeur, and the Glory of the Divine Essence, and the Sublimity of the Realm of Might, and [...] praise be upon my father and what is in my Lord's knowledge!

order.why: Read testimony within the particular practice of visitation.
shortened: When you enter the Blessed Shrine, pray in the small chamber near the abandoned well, then turn towards the Kaaba and say: I bear witness that there is no God but God, alone, with no partner, just as His Essence has testified to His Essence that there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Keep the acknowledgment from a mountain setting in its own voice.
shortened: I bear witness before God, from my station amidst these mountains, that there is no God but Him, alone without partner, even as His Essence hath testified to His Essence in the loftiness of His Being.

order.why: Read self-testimony in the letter to Tahirih.
shortened: O my God! I bear witness before Thee and before those who bear witness in Thy presence that in this Book I testify that there is no God but God, alone without partner, even as He hath testified of His Own Self unto His Own Self, and sanctified His Own Being above any likeness to aught else beside Him. He is as He is in the glory of His Being, the majesty of His Essence, the beauty of His Self, and the sanctity of His Identity.

order.why: Join testimony with knowledge and justice.
Consider the purifying and ascending effects attributed to confession.
Let praise acknowledge its own inadequacy.
shortened: I glorify Thee beyond all wherewith contingent things have glorified Thee or can glorify Thee, and I sanctify Thee beyond all wherewith contingent things have sanctified Thee or can sanctify Thee, and I testify to Thy oneness as Thou hast testified to Thine own oneness, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, and all else besides Thee is Thy creation and within Thy grasp.

order.why: Preserve the prayer’s severe language within its devotional setting.
shortened: Thou didst not create that creation save that all things might attain, to the extent possible, unto that which is manifested at the revelation of Thy power and the exaltation of Thy Will. Perished be the essence that glorifieth not Thy Being, and annihilated be the reality that praiseth not Thine Essence. Extinguished be the spirits that recognize not the Sovereign of Thy holy Oneness, and abolished be the bodies that prostrate not before the Monarch of Thy Unity.

order.why: Read the repeated appeal through the radiance and Tree of oneness.
Follow the long litany asking entry into paradise by mercy.
shortened: O God! I beseech Thee by the sovereignty wherein Thou art unique, O Most Merciful, to grant permission unto me and unto them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, to enter Thy paradise through Thy bounty and Thy mercy.

O God! I beseech Thee, O First One in Thy uniqueness, O Last One, to grant permission unto me and unto them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, to enter Thy paradise through Thy bounty and Thy mercy.

O God! I beseech Thee, O Most Glorious in Thy uniqueness, O Hidden One, to grant permission unto me and unto them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs, to enter Thy paradise through Thy bounty and Thy mercy.

order.why: Consider praise as attraction and strength.
Hear the warning to heed the declaration.
shortened: Say: O servants, take heed! There is none other God but God.
God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, before and hereafter, and all shall return unto Him.

order.why: Turn confession toward concentrated attention.
shortened: Enable them then, O my God, to bear witness to Thy unity and to testify to Thy oneness in such wise that they may behold naught save Thee and shut their eyes to all else.

order.why: Read the instruction to recite its prayer of peerlessness.
Join power and loving-kindness in testimony.
shortened: I testify to Thine omnipotence and Thy might, Thy sovereignty and Thy loving-kindness, Thy grace and Thy power, the oneness of Thy Being and the unity of Thine Essence, Thy sanctity and exaltation above the world of being and all that is therein.

order.why: Keep the short personal prayer denying equal and likeness.
Preserve the distinct confession joining oneness and wisdom.
shortened: O Lord! I testify to Thy oneness and singleness, and that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, the Single, the One, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Address the One as Beloved, Support and Hope.
shortened: O my God, my Beloved, my Lord, my Support, and my Hope! I testify that Thou hast ever been One, Single, Self-Subsisting, Alone, and wilt continue to be what Thou hast always been.

order.why: Let the Dove’s cooing prompt a spoken response.
shortened: When thou hearest the cooing of the Dove of My utterance upon the branches of the Tree of My knowledge, say: "My God, my God! I testify to Thy oneness and Thy singleness, and that Thou hast no partner in Thy dominion nor any equal in Thy kingdom.

order.why: Give thanks for acknowledgment and discernment.
shortened: My God, my God! All praise be to Thee for having caused me to acknowledge Thy oneness and confess Thy singleness, and to submit to that which Thou hast sent down in Thy Book, whereby Thou didst distinguish between truth and falsehood through Thy command and Thy power.

order.why: Join the sending of signs with learning and nearness.
Read recognition, listening and turning as one act of gratitude.
shortened: Say: My God, my God! Unto Thee be praise and unto Thee be thanksgiving, unto Thee be bounty and generosity, for having honored me with Thy days and caused me to recognize the Dawning-Place of Thy Cause, the Manifestation of Thy Self, and the Dayspring of Thy signs, and for having aided me to turn toward Thy most exalted horizon, to hearken unto Thy sweetest call, and to turn toward the lights of Thy countenance, O Lord of all names and Creator of the heavens! O my Lord! Thou seest me turning toward Thee and turning away from all else, acknowledging that which the tongue of Thy grandeur hath spoken when Thou didst establish Thyself upon the throne by Thy command and will, that verily Thou art God, Who hath ever been One, Single, Alone, and Self-Subsisting, and wilt ever remain as Thou hast been.

order.why: Keep the separate thanksgiving for guidance amidst denial.
shortened: When thou hast received My Tablet and been blessed with the Kawthar of My utterance, say: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for having guided me when mankind was in manifest error, and for having caused me to turn toward Thee when the people were in grievous rejection, and for having enabled me to acknowledge the oneness of Thy Being when humanity was in severe denial.

order.why: Preserve the particular address to a handmaiden.
shortened: O My handmaiden! Hearken thou unto My call, then bear witness to that whereunto God did bear witness before the creation of earth and heaven, that there is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Bestower.

order.why: Let the brief acknowledgment of a heard confession stand distinctly.
Keep the letter’s recognition of turning toward the unseen light.
Read another person’s letter as evidence of insight and love.
shortened: O you who are guided by the light of guidance! I have read your missive with its wonderful contents and eloquent meanings, indicating your recognition of the oneness of God and your acknowledgment of His singleness, and the enlightenment of your insight and the purity of your inner being and the intensity of your love for the Beauty of God.

order.why: Notice the joy and fragrance found in another’s acknowledgment.
Preserve the distinction between recognition and learned denial.
shortened: Blessed art thou for having drunk of the Sealed Wine when every heedless one turned away from it veiled, and for having acknowledged the oneness and singleness of God when every rejected learned one denied Him.

order.why: Let each letter of the answering Book bear witness.
Keep the confession made while standing in a particular station.
shortened: I testify that Thou art God, there is none other God but Thee.

Thou beholdest me, O my God, standing in this station, acknowledging Thy oneness and confessing Thy singleness, and I acknowledge that which the tongue of Thy grandeur hath spoken and that which Thy chosen ones have acknowledged.

order.why: Hear the Pen and respond through testimony.
shortened: When thou hearest My most sweet call and the rustling of My Most Exalted Pen, say: O Lord of all beings and Sovereign of the hereafter and of former times! I testify to Thy oneness and Thy singleness and to Thy power, Thy might and Thy dominion.

order.why: Retain the separate call to witness before creation.
Keep the brief collective affirmation of grandeur and sovereignty.
Read First, Last, Manifest and Hidden together.
Preserve the address from the Wronged One to an acknowledging soul.
Keep the separate witness in the Kingdom of Utterance.
Retain the Wronged One’s concise testimony.
Read acknowledgment from the setting of a sorrowful prison.
shortened: Give thanks unto God for having turned unto thee the face of Him Who hath been wronged, from the direction of His sorrowful prison, and Who speaketh and saith: There is none other God but He, the Single, the One, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Preserve the selected interval between testimony and forgiveness.
shortened: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him.
He, verily, is the Single One, the One, the All-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful.

order.why: Keep the concise statement linking testimony and the speaking One.
shortened: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, and He Who speaketh is indeed the Single One, the All-Informed.

order.why: Retain the separate selected intervals concerning sovereignty.
Preserve the repeated testimony around the omitted interval.
Read origin and return through the proclamation of a Day.
shortened: This is the Day wherein the Mystery of Divine Unity hath proclaimed: The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the One, the All-Powerful, the Unconstrained. With Him did the Day begin and with Him shall it end, and from Him have the lights appeared and unto Him have they returned.

order.why: Consider unity’s banner alongside detachment.
shortened: Through them were revealed the mysteries of divine unity, and through them was raised aloft the word of detachment, and through them was hoisted upon the highest standard the banner of "There is none other God but Him."

order.why: Keep the praise and raised banner in their source setting.
shortened: Praise that is sanctified above the comprehension of all created things and the understanding of all beings befits and is worthy of the Lord of names and attributes, Who, to the dismay of the ungodly, has raised aloft the banner of divine unity upon the highest standards and planted the ensign of "Verily He is God" upon the most elevated station.

order.why: Retain the brief opening invocation of that banner.
Read the school of unity beyond ordinary measures of time.
Acknowledge the source’s limit on knowing how this occurs.
shortened: And none knoweth how this is save him whom Thou hast acquainted with the repositories of Thy Oneness and the treasuries of Thine eternity.

order.why: Keep the promised sign of wonder in its own context.
Distinguish signs of glory from veils that obstruct vision.
Ask to be freed from idle fancies in the act of confession.
shortened: I beseech Thee to inscribe me, by Thy Most Exalted Pen, among those who have acknowledged Divine Unity and detached themselves from idle fancies and from that which befitteth not Thy days.

order.why: Connect detachment with readiness to speak the Word of Unity.
shortened: Blessed is the soul whose heart is free and detached from the world and all that is therein. Such a one is worthy to make mention of the blessed Word of Unity.
Praise be to God that the favored community has attained to this station and acknowledges and confesses the oneness of God.

order.why: Keep the prayer for inclusion among the acknowledging ones.
Read the appeal for preservation through yearning and mercy.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the yearning of the hearts of the lovers and the sighs of the hearts of the longing ones, and by Thy Name through which the pavilion of misbelief was destroyed and the canopy of divine unity was raised up, to preserve him who hath believed in Thee and in Thy signs, and hath held fast unto the cord of Thy bounty, and hath turned toward the direction of Thy mercy and Thy good-pleasure.

order.why: Attend to humility and supplication before oneness.
shortened: This is Thy servant who hath bowed down before the King of Thy oneness, who hath humbled himself before the presence of Thy singleness, who hath believed in the Beauty of Thy uniqueness, and who hath supplicated the Kingdom of Thy self-subsistence.

order.why: Seek refuge and the attraction of holy fragrance.
shortened: O our Lord! Send down upon this one who seeketh refuge at the gate of Thy oneness, from the outpourings of the heaven of Thy glorious unity, and attract him through the holy fragrances of Thy singleness.

order.why: Read the departed bird within the garden of forgiveness.
Keep the personal encouragement to hope.
Let acknowledgment stand at mercy’s gate.
shortened: Thus do I acknowledge Thy oneness and confess Thy singleness, submitting to Thy grandeur and Thy sovereignty, and standing before the gate of Thy mercy, turning toward Thy countenance after the passing of the people of Thy kingdom.

order.why: Preserve the prayer’s remembrance of steadfastness and martyrdom.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Thy most exalted Self, and by Thy Most Great Sign, and by Thy Most Beautiful Names, to number me among the people of Thy paradise who have acknowledged Thy oneness and confessed Thy singleness and turned toward the direction of Thy mercy and remained steadfast in Thy remembrance until they were martyred in Thy path and sacrificed themselves in Thy love and good-pleasure.

order.why: Keep the appeal to raise remembered souls into divine good-pleasure.
shortened: I call upon Thee by Thy Name through which Thou didst raise up the heavens upon the thread of Thine eternity and didst elevate the pavilions of the Cause upon the throne of the glory of Thine oneness, that Thou mayest send down upon those who have mentioned Thy Most Exalted Name and who have followed the path of Thy love in the realm below, and then raise them up, O my God, unto the stations of holiness in Thy presence, that they may dwell in Thy habitations and drink from the cup of Thy good-pleasure.

order.why: Imagine a servant becoming a temple of unity.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the beauty of Thy countenance, through which the lights of Thy sun of pre-existence and the splendors of Thy moon of oneness have shone forth upon all created things, that Thou make Thy servant who hath believed in Thee one of the temples of Thy divine unity, and raise him to such a station that he may dwell in the precincts of Thy mercy and rest beneath the shade of Thy loving-kindness.

order.why: Ask for divine qualities and an enkindled heart.
shortened: O Lord! Aid Thy sincere servants to be endowed with the signs of Thy Divine nature and to be inflamed with the fire kindled in the Tree of Thy Oneness.

order.why: Read the fire of oneness as purification from idle fancy.
Connect confession with justice and service amid tyranny.
Bring the prayer to deeds acceptable in the cause of unity.
Ask that hatred be removed so people may become as one soul.
Let the gathered community become a visible sign of oneness.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the dawn of Thy unity which has risen, appeared, shone forth and proclaimed the light of Thy oneness and the mystery of Thy detachment from all peers and likenesses, to unite the scattered members of this gathering beneath the shade of the tree of Thy oneness and to bring together the dispersed of this company under the word of Thy singleness, and make them a sign of Thy oneness, a token of Thy sovereignty, and a flame of Thy light, and a gleaming that has shone forth in the horizons of Thy kingdom.

order.why: Let ocean, ark and fragrance announce an invitation to witness.
Read the resulting joy through the garden and banquet imagery.
Keep the richly patterned birds and gardens as a devotional culmination.
shortened: Praise be to God that the King of power and might is seated upon the throne of glory, and the Sovereign of eternity is established in the realm of meeting, and the sweet-scented breezes of eternity are stirred from the left side of the Beloved's locks, and the fragrant musk of faithfulness wafts from the right side of the Intended One's hair, and the Bird of Light warbles upon the branches of the Tree of Sinai, and the Cock of Glorification sings in the gardens of Divine Unity.

order.why: Pass the water of life among all contingent beings.
Close the linked readings with an invitation both to drink and to give.
Begin the supplied philosophical materials with the provisional account of the Divine Spirit.
Keep Ibn Arabi’s account of indifferentiation in its supplied translation.
Compare al-Qunawi’s distinction between eliminated and established modes.
Read Izutsu’s explanation with its explicit differences among interpreters.
Follow his fuller account of emanation and archetypes without equating it with every preceding text.
shortened: The creative movement, or, to use the technical terminology of wahdat al-wujud philosophy, the self-manifestation (tajalli) of the Absolute which is activated by the principle of love, emerges for the first time at the stage of ahadiyah and is called the 'most sacred Emanation' (Fayd-i-Aqdas). As the result of this Emanation, the stage of wahidiyah becomes established. The wahidiyah, is the ontological state at which the original absolute Oneness of the reality of existence appears with inner articulations. These inner articulations are called, in accordance with the traditional terminology of theology, divine Names and Attributes.
The essential Perfections of God that are thus established in divine Consciousness with clear demarcations are called the 'eternal Archetypes' (a`yan thabitah).

order.why: Preserve the Plotinian excerpt’s relation to Plato and its source omissions.
Consider a One that is not unified by participation in another.
Read the further warning that thought’s unity remains inadequate.
Close with the supplied distinction between existential and manifestational oneness.

questions: What changes when oneness is understood as freedom from comparison rather than simply the number one?
How do the images of painter, sun, mirrors, point, and cloud help thought, and where might each become misleading?
What distinctions do you find among the explanations of essence, names, attributes, and manifestation, including the supplied philosophical excerpts?
How can the confession that God exceeds thought coexist with the language of intimate love, hope, and prayer?
How does the Shema’s integration of love, memory, teaching, and daily life illuminate the devotional passages here?
What might it mean for a gathering to become a sign of oneness, and how could the neighboring subject on idolatry sharpen that inquiry?

references.label: 1 · Deuteronomy 6:4–9 · Oneness remembered in daily life
references.note: Read the Shema’s affirmation alongside the command to love wholeheartedly and remember through speech, teaching, and the home. This passage places divine oneness within Israel’s covenantal life. Compare that practical and devotional emphasis with the compilation’s metaphysical distinctions: how does what one confesses become a rhythm of living?

subjects.displayTitle: War and peace: measuring victory by the life it preserves
subjects.introduction: Twenty years of a parent’s worry and love go into raising a child to full strength, and a battle spends tens of thousands of such lives in an instant. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá keeps returning to that arithmetic: the farmer whose harvest is taxed for cannon, the river made a border though created for both banks, the man who is a murderer if he kills one and a conqueror if he kills a hundred thousand. Victory itself is suspect, two ships colliding and both damaged. The remedy is not exhaustion, which only pauses the next war, but education, the uprooting of prejudice, arbitration before an international tribunal, a pact binding every government to rise against any aggressor, and armaments reduced by common agreement. Beside this stands a careful distinction for the defence of the oppressed, so that the hard questions of holy war and violence in the name of God are faced rather than avoided. Micah’s swords beaten into ploughshares offer a kindred image of strength redirected. The road runs on toward the oneness of humanity and the Lesser and Most Great Peace, and toward the plainer work of turning a sword into a tongue and the noise of the gun into the voice of the Kingdom.
subjects.arc: Begin with human loss and the paradox of victory; examine the material and moral costs of militarism; consider causes, historical warnings and failed settlements; explore justice, collective arrangements and education; end with practical and spiritual forms of peacemaking.

order.why: Introduce the proposal to turn weapons into means of welfare.
shortened: For six thousand years, according to history, there hath ever been war and contention. The fire of battle hath blazed to a mighty height, and every land hath been continually beset with fear and dread. War have we tried, and its results have we beheld: ruin and bewilderment and everlasting loss. Now, according to the divine teachings, let us for a while promote universal peace, and lay the foundation of love and reconciliation among the nations. Let us change weapons into welfare, and transform the instruments of vengeance into implements of husbandry.

order.why: Open with twenty years of care destroyed in an instant.
shortened: With a thousand worries, troubles and tears he raises a child. Then, he readily puts thousands upon thousands of them to the sword's blade. It takes twenty years for a person to grow to maturity and full strength, but in an instant, these people massacre tens of thousands of men and allow them to perish. How many cities are thoroughly destroyed, how many villages are reduced to heaps of dust, how much blood reddens the soil and how immense are the properties that are plundered and wrecked! And yet, there is no benefit in any of this!

order.why: Use colliding ships to unsettle the ordinary meaning of victory.
Follow a farmer’s labor into the continuing financial cost of armaments.
shortened: Today the greatest calamity in the world is war. Humanity has no peace and war is constant, because all nations are continuously preparing for war. All wealth is spent on war. The poor farmer toils day and night with the labor of his hands and sweat of his brow to obtain a few seeds and gather a small harvest, but to what benefit? For the produce goes to war preparations and is spent on cannons, rifles, arsenals and warships. This financial war is constant.

order.why: Question the power of a line drawn across a shared river.
shortened: Man has set up imaginary lines, only to have these become causes of strife. A river is made a boundary, one side called France and the other Germany. The river was in reality created for both. What a superstition! An imaginary line to become a cause of bloodshed!

order.why: Contrast the treatment of an individual killing with the prestige of mass killing.
Keep compassion for those forced into battle near the opening.
shortened: "God treats these people with His mercy, not with His justice, since God is against war. But as many did not will the war, but were obliged to go to the battle field by force of circumstances, therefore God has mercy for they suffered much and they lost their lives.

order.why: Read a young life through its unrealized possibilities.
shortened: War is a grievous calamity. It begins and ends in disaster. A mother has a beautiful boy filled with every grace and promise. He develops into manhood, goes to war, and in an instant all his possibilities sand usefulness are cut off.

order.why: Let trees, lamps and unopened buds make interrupted lives perceptible.
shortened: Consider the torrents of blood shed in the fields of battle for no good cause and for no sane purpose. Consider how many of humanities noble trees have been uprooted in their youth, how many lamps have been extinguished in this world barely after they were ignited, how many multi-coloured buds have been cut down before they had a chance to bloom, before their fragrant blossoms even opened.

order.why: Attend to parents, children and homelessness in the letter’s account.
shortened: The fires of conflict have blazed so high that never in early times, not in the Middle Ages, not in recent centuries hath there ever been such a hideous war, a war that is even as millstones, taking for grain the skulls of men. Nay, even worse, for flourishing countries have been reduced to rubble, cities have been levelled with the ground, and many a once prosperous village hath been turned into ruin. Fathers have lost their sons, and sons their fathers. Mothers have wept away their hearts over dead children. Children have been orphaned, women left to wander, vagrants without a home.

order.why: Keep the separate enumeration of broken family relationships.
Read grief through the specific landscape of France.
Preserve the reported account of mourning in Paris.
Bring family suffering into the address about Tripoli.
shortened: Observe what is taking place in Tripoli: men cutting each other into pieces, bombardment from the sea, attacks from the land and the hail of dynamite from the very heaven itself. The contending armies are thirsting for each other's blood. How they can do this is inconceivable. They have fathers, mothers, children; they are human. What of their wives and families? Think of their anguish and suffering. How unjust, how terrible! Human beings should prevent and forbid this.

order.why: Read the comparison with predatory animals as rhetoric in its historical setting.
Question what a corner of earth can justify.
Keep the separate reported response to the Italian-Turkish war.
Read the poor person’s sacrifice for another’s greed.
Follow territorial attachment into the image of the graveyard.
Preserve the separate address’s elaboration of that image.
Keep the London formulation concerning an eternal cemetery.
shortened: Nations sometimes say, 'We wish to extend our boundaries!' Consider with me for a moment, 'What is the earth?' We live for a few years on its surface and then it becomes our eternal cemetery. Millions of generations are buried there. It is the universal graveyard of humanity. Is it praise worthy to engage in war for a cemetery--to pillage the wealth of nations for an eternal graveyard?

order.why: Set contention against the stated purpose of peace and reform.
Retain the Manchurian setting and the earth-as-serpent image.
Retain the letter’s judgment on conquest by sword and firearm.
Read the stated figures and losses as the source’s historical account.
shortened: Consider how in the wilderness of Manchuria two million souls sacrificed their lives for the sake of earth, and throughout the winter season, in cold and storm and snow and rain, from morn till night they strove with utmost vigor to shed blood in the field of sacrifice. They shall find no fruit save manifest loss.
Indeed, war and strife, battle and conflict, striking and struggling are a disgrace to the human world and prevent prosperity and salvation.

order.why: Notice the estrangement of people ordered to kill strangers.
Set national labels beside shared humanity.
Preserve the reported critique of peace reserved for the weak.
Examine the double standard in the reported comparison with raiding tribes.
shortened: The politicians of the world maintain that war is the cause of material and intellectual progress. Yet they themselves consider the Bedouin Arabs to be contemptible and savage because they raid one another and plunder each other's property, while they themselves do exactly the same thing. The only difference is that the Arabs do this with sword and spear, while they do it with cannon and rifle.
Even if they conquer a country, how can a mother whose children have been killed find any joy or delight in such a victory?

order.why: Follow the criticism of war as a supposed school of courage.
Question a civilization measured by its more destructive weapons.
Imagine civilization without dependence on instruments of terror.
Read the reported contrast between humanity’s natural gentleness and invented weapons.
Consider why modern weapons change the scale of endurance.
shortened: This last terrible war hath clearly proven that humanity cannot withstand the effects of modern instruments of warfare. The future can in no wise be compared to the past, for earlier weapons and armaments had but a feeble effect, whilst modern ones can, in a brief span of time, strike at the very roots of the world of humanity and surpass the limits of its endurance.

order.why: Keep the reported warning concerning weapons carried through the air.
Read the escalating reach of armies and navies in the 1912 address.
shortened: Continual additions to the armies and navies of the world will be made, and the fear and certainty of the great pandemic war -- the war unparalleled in history -- will be intensified; for armament, heretofore limited, is now being increased upon a colossal scale. Conditions are becoming acute, drawing nigh unto the degree of men warring upon the seas, warring upon the plains, warring in the very atmosphere with a violence unknown in former centuries.

order.why: Keep the Paris address’s account of territorial ambition and growing armaments.
Consider civilized countries becoming arsenals.
State the consumption of both people and wealth.
shortened: This day, in the world of humanity, men are all the time expending, for war is nothing but the consumption of men and of wealth.

order.why: Follow the removal of workers from useful occupations.
shortened: War was the greatest calamity that could overtake the nations, because the people usually employed in agriculture, trades, commerce, and other useful arts, were taken away from their various occupations and turned into soldiers, so that there was great waste and loss, in addition to the destruction and carnage of war.

order.why: Keep the letter’s account of ruined commerce and enforced enlistment.
Retain the quoted parliamentary figures as attributed historical claims.
Read the reported comparison of earlier war and the Russo-Japanese conflict.
Keep the vivid description of weapons, fortresses and ruined humanity.
shortened: The fire of war is the flame of rifle and cannon. The fires of battles are the inferno of Krupp. Dragon-like vessels are engaged in attack and battle. The foundation of fortresses is destroyed and buried. Strong castles are leveled to the ground. Troops like waves are drowned and destroyed in the sea of death by incurable demise. Bodies of the slain are rolling in dust and blood. Rivers of blood are flowing and streaming. The foundation of humanity is demolished and ruined.

order.why: Attend to the letter’s stark slaughterhouse comparison.
Let the image of flowing blood and trembling hearts stand in its own source.
Read the wartime letter’s grief and quoted poetry together.
shortened: From the dawn of human history until now, never hath such a soul-consuming flame been kindled, nor such a conflagration spread to all horizons. All eyes are weeping and all hearts are burning. The whole continent of Europe hath become a field of bloodshed and an arena of savagery. As the poet sayeth: "There is not a thorn whose tip is not reddened with the blood of martyrs." Cries and lamentations reach to the zenith of heaven. The tears of orphans flow like floods, while fathers grieve in mourning for their sons.

order.why: Keep the public paper’s account of suffering and destroyed homes.
Keep the retrospective address’s description of war and bereavement.
shortened: O noble friends and seekers for the Kingdom of God!

Some fifty to sixty years ago, when the fire of war was raging amongst governments and nations and bloodshed was considered the greatest of human attainments, the blood of thousands of human souls coloured the earth each day. Children were left without fathers, fathers without their sons, and mothers moaned and wailed, with tearful eyes and burning hearts, at the loss of their children. The darkness of hatred and animosity had enveloped humanity, the heavenly light had completely disappeared, and the breathings of the Holy Spirit were withheld.

order.why: Preserve the separate letter’s description of humanity in mortal combat.
shortened: O ye dear friends! The world is at war and the human race is in travail and mortal combat. The dark night of hate hath taken over, and the light of good faith is blotted out. The peoples and kindreds of the earth have sharpened their claws, and are hurling themselves one against the other. It is the very foundation of the human race that is being destroyed.

order.why: Introduce the shift from religious to racial and patriotic warfare.
Consider the many stated pretexts for recurring conflict.
Connect warfare with ignorance, misunderstanding and failed education.
Keep the synagogue address’s focus on religious misunderstanding.
shortened: From the beginning of human history until this day, there has been strife among humanity, hatred and enmity, war and bloodshed. Why? Because of misunderstandings between religions, misunderstandings that have laid waste the human world. People have shed each other's blood, have taken each other's children captive, have plundered each other's property.

order.why: Read the Balkan example in the Congregational Church address.
Examine religion, patriotism and courage used to disguise aggression.
Keep the interview’s extended account of changing excuses.
shortened: Every hour war is threatened upon some new pretext; today patriotism is its basis, tomorrow religious prejudice, racial egotism, territorial greed, commercial selfishness--it matters little what the excuse may be--blood is shed and human beings torn to pieces upon battlefields. Political interests clash; a great war follows; sadness, gloom and cruelty envelop the world.

order.why: Follow the reported contrast between claims of victory and actual defeat.
shortened: Nations in various ages have resorted to different excuses to slaughter their fellowmen and crown their heads with the bloody crown of so-called victory which we may call it defeat. In the past religious wars were repeatedly waged on the ground that this is Mohamadan, that is Christian, this Hindu, that is a Jew etc. This was a pretext appealed to the religious emotions of mankind. Another excuse has been and is that of country or patriotism, this is France, that is Germany, here is England and that is India. Let my country advance at the expense of another. Let me do something to grab a piece of somebody else's land. Let the commerce of my people develop while the other is ruined!

order.why: Question hostility grounded in thoughts, habits and imagined differences.
Read ignorance and prejudice alongside increasing militarization.
Consider the reported claim that religious war contradicts religion itself.
Bring professed religious kinship into conflict with conduct.
shortened: Nominally speaking the English and the German people belong to the Protestant wing of Christianity while the French and Austrians are Catholics. Notwithstanding this religiou[s] kinship they have already crimsoned many battlefields with the blood of each other. Why the display of this wolf-like quality? Why the appearance of these savage and brute forces?

order.why: Read the drawn sword against Christ’s instruction to Peter.
shortened: In these days the world suffereth from unrest and turmoil, from contention and conflict and mankind is confused and stricken, and yet Christ bade Peter sheath his sword. And though He declared that he that draweth his sword shall by the sword be brought into account, yet notwithstanding, the sword hath been drawn and the peoples of the world are engaged in conflict.

order.why: Keep the reported questions about peacemaking, diplomacy and patriotic incitement.
shortened: Again Christ says: 'Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.' How does this agree with the intrigues of politicians, the machinations of the diplomatists behind the closed doors of their chancelleries and the constant incitement of jingo-press with their Pseudo-patriotism and the Continent of Europe becoming one vast, dangerous arsenal for the combustion of which only one spark is necessary and then there will be a world-consuming conflagration?

order.why: Question the invocation of divine mercy for military victory.
Preserve the newspaper story of competing national prayers as a reported account.
Turn the request for a nation’s victory toward impartial adjudication.
shortened: Some of the German friends have asked that victory be given to Germany. We are not interfering with either party. Here at the Threshold of Baha'u'llah we pray that they may seek Peace and settle all their outstanding disputes before a judicial, impartial, international court.
May they upraise the banner of Universal Peace!

order.why: Keep the direct statement that war opposes the divine will.
shortened: God does not want war. These wars are against the divine will. He desires peace and love for His servants.

order.why: Read the hope of justice with its explicit refusal to attribute this war to God’s desire.
shortened: God willing, the sun of rest and tranquility will soon rise from the horizon of this world, and humanity will repose in the cradle of ease and joy. These are the days of testing, that pure gold may be separated and souls filled with prejudice and disease may vanish. The lights of justice and equity shall shine forth and be freed from the bonds of nature. It is abundantly clear that God, exalted be His glory, did not desire this war and strife.

order.why: Preserve the sweeping reported judgment concerning Russia and Japan with its distinct authority.
Consider the reported image of sacrifice reflected on water.
shortened: Consider how many men are engaged most devotedly in the present War; how they sacrifice and give their lives and possessions; how great is the number of soldiers among them. They are commanded by men who have dedicated their lives to the study of the science of war. They are all ready to sacrifice themselves in an instant. And yet their sacrifice has no benefit. [It is transient,] like a picture reflected on water.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast of enduring remembrance and battlefield anonymity.
shortened: If one soul is martyred for the sake of Truth, eternally shall he shine from the horizon of Glory; but for the last six months probably more than one million living, breathing youths have been left on the battlefields as dead corpses and soon their very names will be forgot[en.] In a few years who will care to know about them as individuals.

order.why: Retain the severe formulation about passing worldly results without using it to diminish victims.
shortened: Now it is thus: millions of souls march forth and perish in the cause of this world, for the sake of countries, either in struggle or in warfare with enemies--it has no importance. Like in these days when so many in Europe are being annihilated, so many fathers are being rendered sonless, so many children fatherless, so many homes are being laid waste, so many mothers throughout the world are crying and lamenting for their children--it has no importance. Soon no trace of it remains.

order.why: Read the particular experience of a war opponent compelled to fight.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha remarked, "Yes, Mousier Bernard was also taken to the battlefield, but if there was a single person in the world who was against war, it was him. He detested it most intensely and was so utterly against it that I am unable to describe for you. However, he was forced into joining the combat. For those who have sacrificed themselves in the path of God, it is difficult to sacrifice instead for mere soil, which is the least worthy of all creation."

order.why: Keep the separate tribute to his opposition to killing.
shortened: His contempt for war was not because he desired to protect his own self, but was due to his hatred of conflict and killing. In truth, he was unique in all human perfections and spiritual attributes. He was a well-wisher for everyone.

order.why: Consider the reported comparison between military discipline and imprisonment.
shortened: Military rules are far worse than prison rules. These soldiers are in reality prisoners. They are restricted in all their affairs. They cannot deviate one hair's breadth from the prescribed rules. They are circumscribed in their eating, sleeping and walking. They are not at all free. Imagination rules over the world of humanity. These men are prisoners in everything save the name. Because they are called soldiers and are summoned to defend what the demagogues call "Fatherland" they willingly go through all these hardships.

order.why: Question leaders’ claims of love when others bear the danger.
Retain the reported attribution of responsibility to rulers.
Hear the rhetorical questions about the purpose of distant armies.
shortened: I have come to find out what you want of me and my people? Why have you caused the shedding of the blood of all these people? For what reason have you ransacked all these cities? Why have you brought these armies from the end of the world to kill and be killed? What is back of this insatiable greed and rapacity?"

order.why: Preserve the reported judgment on failed policies.
shortened: Instead of being the cause of the honor of the world of humanity they will be the means of its debasement. Their policies shall collapse like a 'pack of cards.' Their intellectual weakness and moral imbecility will be exposed.

order.why: Read the account of remorse after reckless entry into war.
shortened: Now that the world is in turmoil, let us see what will happen after this tempest; God willing, it will turn out well. These governments, without remembering the difficulties of this war, or considering its consequences, or taking into account the gravity of the situation, rush recklessly into war. Now both sides are remorseful. Had they known it would come to this, they would not have acted so rashly.

order.why: Consider the temporary victories in the reported Napoleon example.
shortened: Napoleon the Great conquered Germany and brought under his control its domain but to what result! It was only a temporary victory. It ruined the homes of thousands to satisfy the beastly ambition of a single man. In a short while Germany recuperated and avenged the wrongs meted him by striking the terror of his arms into the very heart of France. The great conqueror himself spent his last days in misery [on] the Island of St. Helena.

order.why: Keep the separate assertion that both sides suffer.
Read the contrast with Christ’s peacemaking through the claim that all are vanquished.
Preserve the reported distinction between military defeat and solidarity’s victory.
shortened: Similarly, all these nation[s] who are fighting each other and forming red rivers of the blood of their fellowmen - are defeated - one and all. For all of them are captives in the claws of lust and passion, are prompted by greed and cupidity and are imbued with the spirit of jealousy and hatred. The Army of the oneness of the world of humanity conquers over all, the Flag of Universal Peace shall wave over all; the power of the Divine Graces shall defeat all and the truths of human solidarity will vanquish all.

order.why: Examine war’s glorification in film alongside the violation of agreed protections.
Keep the separate criticism of broken Hague conventions.
Read the reported discrepancy between a peace speech and later war.
shortened: The Czar of Russia promoted The Hague Peace Conference and proposed the decreased in armament for all nations. In this Conference it was proved that Peace was beneficial to all countries, and war destroyed trade, etc. The Czar made a very good speech, though after it was over he, himself, was the first to declare war (against Japan).

order.why: Recall the promising Hague discussions in their own historical setting.
Set peace assemblies beside the ensuing wars.
Read the retrospective list of failed settlements as the reported speaker’s argument.
Keep the reported criticism of incomplete representation in the League of Nations.
shortened: ['Abdu'l-Baha] responded:

Yes, since they have disobeyed the blessed instructions [of Baha'u'llah]. Only a few countries have representatives in the League of Nations, whereas the representatives must be appointed and ratified by the nation, the government, the monarch and the Senate. They do not even consult. On the other hand, some governments are deprived of membership, and this has precipitated their fury and prompted their feeling of revenge. Governments have secret alliances with each other of which no one is aware, but these schemes will reach nowhere.

order.why: Distinguish exhaustion-driven peace from lasting peace.
Read the argument for spiritual education beyond material civilization.
shortened: Praise be to God, in this severe war and grievous torment it became firmly established that nothing but divine teachings are the cause of success and prosperity, and nothing but heavenly law can preserve the human world. This was the outcome of the great civilization that came to pass. Thus it became clear that the comfort and ease of the human world and the protection and preservation of human society is impossible through civilization alone - rather it must be combined with divine teachings, and the human world must be quickened and refreshed by the breaths of the Holy Spirit, and through the power of the Word of God the banner of universal peace must be raised. Otherwise human powers are impotent.

order.why: Use the dessert comparison to examine the low priority given to peace.
Preserve the reported reasoning used to defend colossal armaments.
shortened: In order that they may safeguard their vital interests, independence and honor, they must[,] they argue, keep up these colossal armies and navies to the highest degree of efficiency. They believe they must keep peace amongst themselves at the point of bayonets, forts, machine guns and infernal engines.

order.why: Read the danger of unilateral disarmament in its specific example.
Include the preceding question and examine the proposed simultaneous agreement.
shortened: Question: What is your opinion concerning disarmament?

Answer: Be a general agreement all the governments of the world must disarm simultaneously and at the same time. It will not do if one lays down the arms and the other refuses to do so. The nations of the world must concur with each other concerning this supremely important subject, thus they may abandon together the deadly weapons of human slaughter.

order.why: Introduce collective restraint of aggression through the address to monarchs.
Consider responsibility for restraining conflict beyond one’s own immediate interests.
Read the Pact, its collective enforcement, and the distinction concerning protective war together.
shortened: The fundamental principle underlying this solemn Pact should be so fixed that if any government later violate any one of its provisions, all the governments on earth should arise to reduce it to utter submission, nay the human race as a whole should resolve, with every power at its disposal, to destroy that government. Should this greatest of all remedies be applied to the sick body of the world, it will assuredly recover from its ills and will remain eternally safe and secure.

A conquest can be a praiseworthy thing, and there are times when war becomes the powerful basis of peace, and ruin the very means of reconstruction. If, for example, a high-minded sovereign marshals his troops to block the onset of the insurgent and the aggressor, or again, if he takes the field and distinguishes himself in a struggle to unify a divided state and people, if, in brief, he is waging war for a righteous purpose, then this seeming wrath is mercy itself, and this apparent tyranny the very substance of justice and this warfare the cornerstone of peace.

order.why: Join care for the broken with restraint of an oppressor.
Preserve the distinction between fighting for justice and fighting from hatred or plunder.
shortened: Even some of them fought against people, but their fighting was not like the fighting of other persons - rather it was based on justice and fairness. But the warfare of people in general stems only from hatred and enmity or worldly conquest. How different these are, when that fighting was to establish justice and fairness, prevent oppressors from tyranny and execute retribution, while this fighting springs from doubt, evil whisperings, love of base desires, plunder and raids.

order.why: Keep the discussion of defense and women’s exemption in its stated wording and context.
Read the lifting of the ordinance of holy war.
Set the reported warning that war begets war beside the preceding distinctions.
Introduce an international tribunal for disputes.
Use the analogy with judicial settlement within a community.
Retain the reported alternative course proposed for Russia and the Hague.
Give arbitration priority over the sword in the reported counsel.
shortened: In this century the voices of peace must drown the clamors for battle, and the principle of arbitration must gain sway over the arbitrement [sic] of the sword. Man must learn war no more neither must he let the brutal and barbaric forces of passion and lust control the humane intellectual and moral powers.

order.why: Imagine the limited security needs of nations within an agreed peace.
shortened: Arms and armaments will, then, be no more needed beyond that which is necessary to insure the internal security of their respective countries. If they attain unto this all-surpassing blessing, the people of each nation will pursue, with tranquillity and contentment, their own occupations, and the groanings and lamentations of most men would be silenced.

order.why: Keep the separately reported account of reduced military requirements.
Preserve the reported recollection of a conversation with a weapon’s inventor.
Restore the question before the answer on humanity’s greatest need.
Keep question and answer together in the call for education in peace.
Retain the brief reported response on public education.
Give schools and universities a responsibility for forming peacemakers.
