Consider the address’s connection between equal education, women’s equality and peace.
Make understanding the harms of war and benefits of peace explicit.
Read the reported proposal to develop effective public opinion.
Consider the manner as well as the content of speech about peace.
Let the tongue replace the worn sword in the reported image.
shortened: The sword has been working over six thousand years and has become dull. We must look about us for another sword to take its place.
The greatest sword is the tongue.

order.why: Contrast coercive obedience with willing response to love.
Read that distinction within the reported conversation with the German Consul.
Return to misunderstanding and the search for religious foundations.
Consider the destruction of long achievement within a single year.
shortened: For strife and warfare are the very destroyers of human foundations, whereas peace and amity are the builders and safeguards of human welfare. As an instance, two nations which have remained at peace for centuries declare war against each other. What destruction and loss befalls both in one year of strife and conflict -- the undoing of centuries. How urgent their necessity and demand for peace, with its comfort and progress, instead of war, which blasts and destroys the foundation of all human attainment.

order.why: Keep the Cedric address’s contrast between human perfection and savagery.
Read love as a social bond in the Westminster address.
Retain the separate overview of continuing warfare.
Keep the compact reported description of a bloodstained history.
shortened: History is a record of incessant wars. There is not a spot on the globe that has not been crimsoned with the blood of men; the whole earth is blood-drenched.

order.why: Hear the Columbia address’s invitation to try another course.
shortened: For thousands of years we have had bloodshed and strife. It is enough; it is sufficient. Now is the time to associate together in love and harmony. For thousands of years we have tried the sword and warfare; let mankind for a time at least live in peace.

Review history and consider how much savagery, how much bloodshed and battle the world has witnessed. It has been either religious warfare, political warfare or some other clash of human interests. The world of humanity has never enjoyed the blessing of universal peace.

order.why: Read the experimental proposal in the interview with Hudson Maxim.
Keep the separate London formulation of the peace experiment.
shortened: During the last six thousand years nations have hated one another, it is now time to stop. War must cease. Let us be united and love one another and await the result. We know the effects of war are bad. So let us try, as an experiment, peace, and if the results of peace are bad, then we can choose if it would be better to go back to the old state of war! Let us in any case make the experiment.

order.why: Give the brief invitation to exercise love room to resonate.
shortened: For thousands of years the human race has been at war. It is enough. Now let mankind, for a time at least, consort in amity and peace. Enmity and hatred have ruled. Let the world, for a period, exercise love.

order.why: Preserve the retrospective account of warnings in the letter.
shortened: Nearly fifty years ago, Baha'u'llah promulgated teachings and raised the call of universal peace. In all His Tablets and epistles, He explicitly foretold these present events, warning that humanity was in grave danger and that a universal war was impending and inevitable, for the inflammable materials stored in the infernal arsenals of Europe would be ignited by a single spark.

order.why: Read the arsenal-and-spark warning in its own source.
Keep the Sacramento address’s warning during the Balkan crisis.
Retain the reported recollection of warnings in synagogues and churches.
Preserve the separate Finkelstein conversation’s account.
shortened: In the course of My journey in the western countries, in all the synagogues and churches, I cried out that Europe was in grievous danger. It was like a barrel of gunpowder that with the least spark would explode and scorch everything in its grasp. I said to them, 'People, exert your efforts to protect humanity from this peril.

order.why: Keep the later reported warning concerning unimplemented teachings.
Read the specific prediction reported in the conversation with Counsel Schwartz.
Preserve the reported statement concerning America’s noninvolvement with its date and authority visible.
Read the reported prophetic interpretation as an interpretation in its historical setting.
shortened: It is said that he poured it on the air, because the air fills every place, and the continuing verses mean the Great War that is to come. After this war everything will be at peace. The city which was cut in three pieces means that kingdom of Babylonia, which is under three kings, those of England, Persia and Turkey. The islands and mountains of v. 20 mean people of influence, and also small kingdoms, which will be destroyed and annihilated at that time.

order.why: Keep the letter’s account of peace assemblies alongside its statement of predestination.
shortened: Through the concerted efforts of some wealthy individuals in America, great assemblies were established to promulgate universal peace and to abolish ruinous warfare and the needless shedding of blood. In spite of this, war was predestined to occur.

order.why: Read the Balkan destruction in the farewell address aboard the Celtic.
shortened: Consider what is happening in the Balkans. Human blood is being shed, properties are destroyed, possessions pillaged, cities and villages devastated. A world-enkindling fire is astir in the Balkans. God has created men to love each other; but instead, they kill each other with cruelty and bloodshed.

order.why: Keep the Washington address’s response to the same crisis.
shortened: Consider events in the Balkans today where a great conflagration of war is furiously raging and so much blood is being shed. Virtually the whole world of humanity is mourning and lamenting because of the revival of these calamitous conditions.

order.why: Preserve the Oakland address’s hope for American efforts.
Keep the letter’s concern for violated human rights.
Read the reported invitation to help establish Balkan peace.
Retain the reported account of war on multiple fronts and new technologies.
Keep the grief-filled language addressed to Ahmad Sohrab.
Read the theatrical metaphor as a reported response to world war.
Preserve the reported image of armed nations rushing like serpents.
Attend to the loss of correspondence and connection.
Keep the particular explanation for a lapse in news.
Read the separate account of distress caused by interrupted letters.
Extend that disruption to the Caucasus and Russia in its source setting.
Notice reopened paths and renewed communication after war.
Keep thanksgiving for received letters and reported protection.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! After the quieting of the fires of war, four letters arrived from you in succession. Since they brought news of the health and safety of the divine friends, they caused the utmost joy. Praise be to God that in this great tempest, the Ship of the Covenant reached the shore of salvation. The danger was severe and there was cause for fear and trepidation, yet through divine protection the friends in all regions remained safe and preserved, especially in the Holy Land where tribulations and dangers were without limit.

order.why: Read the contrast between general suffering and the letter’s account of protection.
shortened: In those days when the fire of war was aflame and the homes of the world's people were burned, when earthquake struck the foundations of the world, when the earth was stained red with the blood of precious youth, when structures collapsed and edifices were destroyed, when millions of mothers tore their collars in mourning for their sons and cried out with tear-filled eyes, when millions of fathers lost their sons and millions of sons lost their fathers, when orphans were left destitute and grief-stricken women became confused and distressed - in such times, the light of the Ancient Beauty's protection shone upon the friends in all regions.

order.why: Preserve the separate testimony of divine protection without generalizing it beyond the source.
Join gratitude with a prayer for every person.
shortened: I praised the Lord for having protected the friends all throughout the war that has now subsided. All mankind was held in the grip of anguish, and calamities afflicted every soul, while the safety of the friends constituted one of the greatest gifts. For that we thank God and pray that He may confer upon every one that which will illumine the hearts, refresh the souls, bestow light to the eyes and brighten the visions; and that is the dawn of the Sun of the Truth upon all regions, from the horizon of universal peace.

order.why: Keep thanksgiving for steadfastness and the light of peace.
Read the hope that fighting will cease in East as well as West.
shortened: Now that the flames of war have been extinguished in the West, God willing they will be completely quenched in the East as well. I hope that rest and tranquility will be achieved.

order.why: Attend to the moment of armistice discussions.
Distinguish the faint ray of peace from its full dawn.
shortened: The dark cloud of war has somewhat dissipated from the world's horizon and a faint ray of universal peace has dawned. Through the favors of the Lord of Hidden Bounties, it is hoped that the brilliant sun of peace and tranquility will shine radiantly from the dawning-place of hopes.

order.why: Read the guarded beginning of peace and the hope for its completion.
shortened: O esteemed souls! Praise be to God that the fire of war has been extinguished in most lands and peace and tranquility have, to some degree, been established. Through God's favors, my hope is that this fire will be completely quenched and that the banner of peace and concord will wave over all horizons. Although this is but the beginning of the dawn of universal peace, I hope that through divine assistance and grace its radiant sun will rise and illumine all horizons with the light of unity, harmony and the Most Great Peace.

order.why: Imagine European peoples living within one homeland.
shortened: May the different nations of Europe attain the station of one nation, and may the continent of Europe become one homeland, so that after this terrible war, perfect harmony, unity and love may be established among all the peoples of Europe.

order.why: Preserve the reported hope for identities and public attitudes transformed.
Keep the reported expectation that suffering will increase desire for peace.
shortened: This War is indeed ruinous and devastating in its effects. However, afterwards, the number of peace-loving people will grow considerably, and the commotions, uproars and the mighty tumult will precipitate [universal] peace.

order.why: Read the war-as-instrument claim as an account of possible awakening, not a prescription for war.
Connect the hoped-for change with active service.
shortened: Now that calm and assurance have been attained, one must charge forth like a fierce lion and valiant hero in the arena of sacrifice, for through this sudden war humankind has developed an intense receptivity, and the loftiness of divine teachings, the luminosity of divine laws, and the contents of divine tablets have been realized. We hope that the universal war will lead to universal peace, and that this bloodshed and violation and recklessness will yield purity and freedom. May the world find rest and the universe adornment. May the tumult of conflict and war be transformed into the jubilation of melody and song.

order.why: Retain the concise statement of humanity’s need after destruction.
shortened: Now all humanity has realized that war is the destroyer of human foundations and mankind is in need of universal peace and likewise in need of other divine teachings.

order.why: Contrasts peace’s constructive results with war’s destruction.
Read the letter’s retrospective claims and contrast between war and peace.
shortened: What was addressed to Berlin and the German Emperor in the Kitab-i-Aqdas was fulfilled, and likewise what was addressed to Constantinople and the Ottoman Sultan was fulfilled, as well as the other blessed utterances in the Surih of the Temple, until all creation became convinced in heart and soul that the Great War is the cause of destruction while peace is the cause of prosperity; war demolishes the edifice of humanity while peace establishes the divine foundation; war is death while peace is life; war is satanic suggestions while peace is divine inspirations.

order.why: Let the Tablet to the Hague gather the contrasts into a full vision.
Connect peace with prosperity, affection and life.
Connect ending prejudice with preventing the destruction of families.
Explore the broad remedy for religious, racial and national estrangement.
Keep the prayer for removal of causes of dissension.
Read the dedication required of those serving peace.
Make the search for ways to extinguish war a shared undertaking.
Imagine the community as a river that puts out the fire.
Keep the reported direct call to quench it.
Retain the San Francisco appeal to become an instrument of peace.
Read perseverance through difficulty as part of that undertaking.
shortened: We must not fear difficulties and labor. They lead us to the noblest end. We must resist the whole world, for the world wants war; unite our efforts and with divine love we will succeed.

order.why: Let the reported contrast of destruction and construction clarify one’s response.
Bring peacemaking into the discipline of thought.
Turn from success at another’s expense toward fellowship.
shortened: That is, each one tears open the breast of another, and sees their own success in another's bitterness, and seeks their own unity in another's estrangement.
Give up war and sharp claws, make peace your aim and seek culture and uprightness. Seek security and peace, and spread wide the feast of fellowship.

order.why: Keep the short sequence from strife to unity.
Read transformation as the aim of spiritual action.
Give service the image of a field of battle becoming a place of meeting.
shortened: My hope is that you will be successful in outstanding services and become the cause of spreading universal peace, so that these fields of war and strife may be transformed into gatherings of fellowship, meeting, love and harmony.

order.why: Imagine a spiritual spring after the autumn of war.
Keep the letter’s description of constructive work during wartime.
Read the letter’s contrast between war and fellowship across East and West.
Read the image of a community shining like the morning star.
shortened: At such a time when the flames of war are burning in East and West, those friends are engaged in the remembrance of God and striving to awaken souls, purify hearts, establish the foundation of unity and harmony between nations, and create affection between East and West, so that the oneness of the world of humanity may shine like a lamp in the gathering of the horizons.
Praise be to God that in the dark night you are illumined, and in these days when the clouds of war have covered the horizons, you are shining like the morning star.

order.why: Contrast the earthly and heavenly colonels in the letter’s imagery.
Preserve the separate distinction concerning a commander’s aims.
Let the heavenly colonel prepare a feast of reconciliation.
shortened: O heavenly Colonel! Leave the battle line and adorn the gathering of peace. Abandon the field of combat and prepare the feast of reconciliation. Take up the cup of friendship and in the assembly of truth pour forth the wine of concord, so that all the peoples of the world may enter beneath the pavilion of love, unity and universal peace. Demolish the foundation of discord and beautify the palace of harmony and fairness.

order.why: Join prayer with practical efforts to protect people from carnage.
Consider assemblies and spiritual fellowship as foundations for peace.
shortened: Organize ye spiritual assemblies; lay ye the foundation of union and concord in this world; destroy ye the fabric of strife and war from the face of the earth; construct ye the temple of harmony and agreement; enkindle ye the light of the realm of the oneness of humanity; open ye your eyes; gaze and behold ye the other world! The Kingdom of peace, salvation, uprightness and reconciliation is founded in the Invisible World, and it will by degrees become manifest and apparent through the power of the Word of God!

I supplicate God that ye may become the army of that Kingdom, in order that by the power of the Most Great Name, the friends of God may conquer this world through love, friendship and the strength of the Kingdom of peace; the human race become compassionate, and bloodshed and carnage be completely effaced from the universe.

order.why: Read the reported prospect of an army equipped with different powers.
shortened: As the Master was looking upon this seemingly victorious army he said: "The wise man sees that another army with no cannons or rifles but with quite other armaments shall defeat this Army. The day is coming when all these armies and regiments are vanquished by the ever-victorious army of the Kingdom of Abha and theirs shall be the glorious triumphs of Peace and brotherhood.

order.why: Keep the sword-to-olive-bough image in its reported account.
Imagine one melody arising from former instruments of conflict.
Follow the transformation of warships and weapons toward trade and cultivation.
shortened: May the dark clouds of war and strife disperse, may the lights of the Sun of Reality shine from the horizon of peace and reconciliation upon all the world, may the light of guidance shine forth, may hearts be illumined, may souls be quickened with eternal life, may the heavenly teachings that have been issued in this luminous century spread, may the foundation of hatred and enmity be destroyed, may the palace of fellowship and love be raised up, may warships be transformed into merchant vessels, may implements of war become tools of agriculture and cultivation, may the fire of oppression and aggression be extinguished, may the breeze of providence blow, may the springtime of the unity of the human world pitch its tent at the pole of the earth, and may the banner of universal peace be raised.

order.why: Keep the brief tribute to amity and joy.
shortened: He abhorred the darkness of war and conflict and praised the light of amity and the spirit of joy and delight.

order.why: Let the reported question imagine fellowship in place of weapons.
shortened: See how bloodthirsty mankind is, see how cruel man is, how heedless of God he is.

Now if instead of sword and saber and bullet and rifle and cannon, they would engage in love and affection and pleasure and delight and celebration and joy, and become intoxicated with the wine of gladness at the feast of fulfillment, and embrace each other as intimate companions harmonious with the angel's song - would that not be better?

order.why: Read the reported hope for security from aggression in the Islamic world.
Preserve the reported hope for a Parliament of humanity.
Keep the reported assurance of support for peacemakers.
Read the reported promise of the Most Great Peace with its source omissions visible.
shortened: Yea, thus shall it be: these fruitless strifes, these ruinous wars shall pass away and the "Most Great Peace" shall come... Do you not also need this in Europe? Is this not what Christ foretold?... The kings and rulers, instead of expending your wealth and treasures for the betterment of countries and the comfort of the people, spend all in the destruction of humankind.... These strifes and this bloodshed and discord must cease, and all men be as one kindred and one family....

order.why: Preserve the correspondent’s question about whether war will give way to fellowship.
shortened: You had expressed complaint about the war and strife, the battles and killing in the lands of Africa, and had voiced your regret, asking whether this unceasing enmity of the proud ones, continuing through ages and cycles, would persist, or whether the beloved beauty of fellowship and love would one day appear in the gathering of the world.

order.why: Let the yearning for another world draw the sequence toward prayer.
shortened: There is war among the religions; war among the nations; war among the peoples; war among the rulers. What a welcome change would it be, if only these black clouds would lift from off the skies of the world, so that the light of reality could be shed abroad! If only the darksome dust of this continual fighting and killing could settle forever, and the sweet winds of God’s loving-kindness could blow from out the wellspring of peace. Then would this world become another world, and the earth would shine with the light of her Lord.

order.why: Keep the appeal for mercy amid an overwhelming war.
shortened: O Lord! The factions have penetrated deep into the fields of struggle and conflict, and this sweeping torrent and grinding war cannot be halted save through Thy mercy which embraceth all that was and shall be.

order.why: Name the bloodshed, ruined homes and severed roads within prayer.
Close by inviting others to join the work and prayer for peace.

questions: How do the images of the bereaved parent, the farmer, and the damaged ship change what counts as victory or loss?
What assumptions about territory, national identity, courage, or progress do these passages ask us to examine?
How would you compare the passages on collective security and protective defense with those condemning warfare, attending to their setting and authority?
What distinguishes a pause caused by exhaustion from a peace sustained by education, institutions, justice, and changed relationships?
In Micah’s image of weapons becoming tools of cultivation, what is being redirected besides metal, and where do you see corresponding possibilities in this compilation?
How might inner discipline, public speech, community life, and international cooperation contribute together to the peace envisioned in the connected subjects?

references.note: Micah places nations learning divine ways beside weapons remade for cultivation and households living without fear. Compare this prophetic vision with the compilation’s concern for education, arbitration, and the redirection of resources. What connections emerge between peace among nations and the security of ordinary daily life?

subjects.displayTitle: ‘Abdu’l‑Bahá’s Western journeys: distance overcome by love
subjects.introduction: He wrote one letter while walking in a New York park because there was no other free moment, and another on a steamship whose rolling made the pen unsteady. After forty years of confinement, ‘Abdu’l‑Bahá, elderly and unwell, crossed seas and continents to speak of peace and the oneness of humanity in churches, synagogues and public halls, and to meet people he had long loved by correspondence. He told the friends in California that no one in history had travelled so far simply to see his friends, and that the distance had seemed carpeted with silk. The journeys are full of ordinary things: electric signs on Broadway, a lakeside hotel, schedules changed, illness, sleepless nights, money refused, the homesick ache for the East. Beneath them runs a single intention, to show by action what teaching means, and a trust that seeds sown in haste would grow after he had gone. Luke’s account of messengers sent out to carry peace into the homes that receive them offers a way to think about travel as service. From here the road continues into ‘Abdu’l‑Bahá’s own account of his life, the stories told of him, and the growth of the Cause that followed.
subjects.arc: Begin with letters in motion, friendship and freedom after confinement; follow invitations, preparation and encounters across the West; attend to practical costs and bodily limits; return through remembrance, results and hopes for further service.

order.why: Open with a letter written while walking because no quiet time remains.
Carry personal remembrance onto the moving steamship.
shortened: Now that I am on the Greatest Ocean, traveling and moving on a steamship amidst the waves, I have thought of you and am writing this letter, though writing is difficult due to the motion of the ship.

order.why: Let the reported welcome of friends dispel fatigue.
Set the meeting in San Francisco against forty years of confinement.
Introduce the fruitful tree and a message expressed in different tongues.
shortened: I desired to become a sturdy and strong and fruitful tree in the Garden of the Blessed Perfection. In this manner I wished to gain growth and development, produce fruits for the healing of nations, deliver the Word of God and unfurl the banner of Reality. Day and night I worked, taught and rested not. In various tongues and under different expressions and sundry terminologies I presented to the world the same eternal message and voiced forth the same truth.

order.why: Pause at dawn on a New York avenue.
Read the reported arrival through liberty, skyline and wonder.
Keep the small remembered response to electric signs.
shortened: As we drove up Broadway, glittering with its electric signs, He spoke of them smiling, apparently much amused.

order.why: Let the longing to meet explain the distance to Los Angeles.
shortened: Where is Acca -- where is Los Angeles? These regions are far away, what vast distances between them and you, distance indeed; but consider how I longed to see you wherefore, I traverse such distances across country and ocean; otherwise this great distance between Los Angeles and the far East was impossible for me, but because of excessive longing, I came.

order.why: Read the reported transformation of a great distance into something near.
shortened: I have crossed 12 or 13,000 miles to come here and see you. The distance is very great. This will show you how much I longed to meet you, and all this distance the roads were as though carpeted with silk. While the sea was rolling and surging it was as though it were smooth and calm. The great Atlantic to my sight was like unto a lake, and from New York to San Francisco it was like unto a mile.

order.why: Preserve the geographical and historical claims as part of the reported expression of love.
shortened: Consider what love Baha'u'llah has created in the hearts, when from the other side of the world - from Syria - I have hastened to the uttermost part of the earth to meet you, and have traveled half of the sphere, of the globe. Considered from a geographical standpoint, there is no further point than San Francisco. You see, this is just the opposite point of Syria. Half an arc has been covered. How great was my longing! This is the love that Baha'u'llah has made possible.

order.why: Keep the simple reported desire to know the friends.
Read the journey as freedom following long confinement.
Introduce the letter’s overview of travel and the message of peace.
shortened: This prisoner of forty years, following his freedom, traveled for three years--from 1910 to the end of 1913--throughout Europe and the vast continent of America. Despite extreme weakness and fatigue, he delivered extensive addresses in all cities, in great gatherings and major churches, proclaiming aloud whatsoever was contained in the Tablets and teachings of Baha'u'llah concerning war and peace.

order.why: Read the reported summary of the journey’s unifying purpose.
Give the journey its stated prayer for a single ideal of service.
Consider the reported intention to demonstrate teaching through action.
Keep the letter’s explanation of limited freedom of thought in Iran.
shortened: My intention was that since freedom of thought is scarce in Iran and Iran is sick and those in authority are averse to the physician, therefore there is no choice but to journey to the West.

order.why: Read the first European effort through weakness, questions and promised assistance.
shortened: The intention was that despite utmost weakness, a mighty call might be raised, hoping for the aid and favor of the Blessed Beauty - otherwise what power has this feeble gnat, what strength and might has this atom of poverty and evanescence?

Day and night were spent in questions and answers, and some souls were stirred by the breeze from the Abha Paradise. Gatherings were formed and meetings arranged, and 'Abdu'l-Baha, through the aid and favor of Baha, uttered a few words according to his weakness. But as the promised confirmation was evident, it influenced spirits and hearts like the melody of the lute and harp.

order.why: Retain the brief announcement of the European journey.
Notice the interruption at Alexandria caused by illness.
shortened: In truth, it had been my intention to travel from Port Said to Marseilles in order to see your luminous faces and spend some days with the friends in that land and region. However, as soon as I boarded the vessel my condition changed such that I had to disembark in Alexandria.

order.why: Keep the invitation to meet before the proposed European stay.
Read the personal letter to a sister from the Swiss lakeside.
Attend to scenery, weather and the continued thought of service.
shortened: It is truly a delightful place. The mildness of the weather, the freshness of the grass and fields, the lushness and pleasantness of the hills, as well as the beauty of the scenery are most perfect. From the day I left Iran until now I had not seen such a place.
Day and night we are thinking of how we can render, through the aid and favour of the Blessed Beauty, may My spirit be a sacrifice for the Threshold of His Dust, some small service.

order.why: Follow the response in Europe toward invitations from America.
Keep the reported invitation from groups concerned with justice and economics.
Read the abundance of invitations beside a heart still turned toward the East.
shortened: Praise be to God, the lights of the Morn of Oneness are spreading throughout all regions with utmost diffusion, and detailed letters, some adorned with a thousand names, arrive from America, and special correspondence comes from both friend and stranger, and communications arrive continually from the great assemblies of America, all requesting 'Abdu'l-Baha's journey to those regions and showing the utmost eagerness and desire. Therefore am I compelled to undertake this journey. Yet my heart is in the East, for it is the Dawning-Point of the Sun of Truth, and my soul and conscience are gladdened and rejoiced in remembrance of the divine friends in Iran.

order.why: Preserve the particular list of inviting gatherings and people.
shortened: From the Universal Peace Conference of America, from the Race Unity Conference, from the Governor of Boston, America, from the great and eminent ones of that land, from its notable figures, and from the friends, letters of invitation are arriving continuously. Therefore I am compelled to journey to America despite great physical weakness and exhaustion from the abundance of work and writing and staying awake at night.

order.why: Keep the letter’s further account of invitations and impending departure.
shortened: O Afnans of the Blessed Tree! 'Abdu'l-Baha will be departing for distant lands in these two days.

The people of America, both friends and strangers, are all pleading with utmost insistence for 'Abdu'l-Baha's presence. Perhaps more than a thousand letters have arrived from the friends and various assemblies of America, even from some church ministers. Therefore I am compelled to make this journey.

order.why: Notice the reported joy in Boston and Malden before arrival.
Read the named friends and daughters within a direct letter of longing.
shortened: To the divine friends in America - Mr. Roy Wilhelm, Mr. and Mrs. McNutt, Mr. and Mrs. Kinney, Mr. Mountford Mills, Mrs. May Maxwell, Mrs. Elizabeth Nurse, Mrs. Ellen Goodall, Mrs. Agnes Parsons, Mr. and Mrs. Hoar, Mrs. Ellen Revonda, Mrs. Krug, Mrs. Ella Cooper, Mrs. Count, Mrs. Charlotte Bingham:

O my kind friends and dear daughters! Despite physical weakness and inability to endure travel, out of utmost longing to see the faces of the friends, 'Abdu'l-Baha is setting out on a journey to that distant country which is like another world, to cross the great ocean and illuminate his eyes with the sight of the friends' faces.

order.why: Consider the decision to cross the sea despite physical weakness.
shortened: In these days I am determined to journey to America, as invitations are arriving continuously from gatherings of friends and strangers alike, and from scientific, political and general assemblies in America. Although this weak body has absolutely no strength to endure sea travel and there is danger of peril, especially in the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, yet hope lies in the confirmations of the Blessed Beauty, that He may make a feeble gnat into a soaring eagle, and a weak ant into a manifest serpent.

order.why: Keep the distinct resolve for a sacrificial movement in America.
shortened: This was the purpose of the European journey, and now, despite weakness, I have determined to undertake the difficult journey to America, so that perhaps, God willing, a sacrificial movement may occur there.

order.why: Read the coming journey as an opportunity for service.
shortened: Therefore, God has arranged circumstances such that 'Abdu'l-Baha travels to the land of the foreigners and hastens to America in the spring, that perhaps he may draw a breath in service to the Sacred Threshold.

order.why: Connect departure with the banner of human oneness.
Let the image of a drop in the ocean of service express intention.
shortened: In these days Abdul-Baha is preparing for departure to the Western lands, that perhaps he may render a sacrificial service at the Sacred Threshold of the Blessed Beauty, and perhaps he may succeed in offering a drop from the ocean of servitude.

order.why: Keep the brief statement of setting out in servitude.
Preserve the concise hope of an American journey.
shortened: God willing, I shall make a journey to America.

order.why: Retain the separate notice of impending travel.
shortened: I am now about to journey to America.

order.why: Keep the promise of a spring departure in its own letter.
Read an earlier postponement and hope for the following year.
Preserve the proposed return to Egypt before another attempt.
shortened: Therefore, I must return to Egypt, and I hope that in the spring no obstacles will arise so that with the utmost joy and fragrance I may hasten to America solely to meet the friends, that the means of happiness may be provided and the glad-tidings of the Abha Kingdom may encompass all.

order.why: Keep the separate announcement of a projected American journey after returning eastward.
Read the burden of responsibilities when travel was not possible.
Keep the difficulty of a winter visit as stated.
Consider comfort and the completion of study in arrangements for other travelers.
Retain the deferment of another person’s visit because of departure.
Keep the particular permission and request for prayer at a holy place in the source’s wording.
Read preparations in Egypt amid repeated invitations.
shortened: O steadfast and firm one! It is several days since I arrived in the land of the Moon of Canaan, and I am preparing for the journey to America, as invitations keep arriving continuously from leaders, prominent figures and associations there with utmost insistence and persistence. Therefore, I must inevitably undertake the journey at the beginning of Naw-Ruz.

order.why: Acknowledge the companions arranging means of travel.
shortened: O ye who are firm in the Covenant! Jinab-i-Munadi-i-Haqq Mirza Munir has opened his tongue in praise and adorned his letter stating that these nine partners have exerted their utmost effort and prepared the means for travel so that I may hasten to the divine regions and raise the call of the Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the proposed route and promise of a departure telegram.
shortened: In accordance with your request, God willing, efforts will be made to depart for America in March, and at the time of departure a telegram will be sent to you either from Alexandria or Naples.
I will depart directly from Alexandria to America and will not go to Europe.

order.why: Preserve the dated sailing plan through Naples.
Read the discovery of a direct ship and expected arrival.
shortened: Now a ship has been found to travel directly from Alexandria to Naples and from Naples to America, that I may see the faces of the friends and be gladdened by meeting the loved ones. But the ship departs from Alexandria on March 25th. God willing, we will arrive in New York around mid-April.

order.why: Keep the separate notice naming the Cedric.
Connect the planned sailing with a proposed Ethical Society meeting.
Retain the brief notice written two days before boarding.
Keep the separate apology for brevity immediately before travel.
Invite prayer for a long journey beyond bodily endurance.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha's desire from all is that they supplicate day and night at the threshold of the Abha Beauty and pray for my support and confirmation in this perilous journey, for the journey is long and this body has no endurance for the rolling of the sea and hardship of the desert.

order.why: Read the passengers’ interest aboard the liner.
Preserve the reported assertion about the voyage’s purpose and novelty as attributed.
shortened: Up to the present time no one has traveled, with a purpose like ours, from Persia to America. Some have made the journey but it was for their personal gain or for trivial motives. Ours may be said to be the first voyage of Easterners to America.

order.why: Keep the brief reported acknowledgment of illness at boarding.
shortened: In any case, I had great longing to meet you. If this longing did not exist, the favor of the Blessed Beauty would not have encompassed me. Although when I boarded the ship in Alexandria I was not well at all.

order.why: Read the New York welcome through the decision to come despite advice.
shortened: I was in Egypt and was not feeling well, but I wished to come to you in America. My friends said, "This is a long journey; the sea is wide; you should remain here." But the more they advised and insisted, the greater became my longing to take this trip, and now I have come to America to meet the friends of God.

order.why: Let the short notice of safe arrival stand distinctly.
shortened: O Amata'l-Baha! With utmost ease I arrived in New York.

order.why: Keep the address to newspaper readers concerning the ocean crossing.
Read the reported recollection of choosing the Cedric rather than the Titanic.
Preserve the account of renewed strength and meetings after arrival.
Keep the bishop’s reported response in its own voice.
Read the remembered Indian visitor’s surprise at an affirmation of Muhammad in a church.
shortened: Once, when I was on my way to speak in a church in New York city, a person from India, a man prominent in that city, met us accidentally. He was surprised and said to himself, 'I will go and see what all this is about.' He came to the church and saw me standing on the platform, proving the prophethood of his holiness the Messenger of God. Indeed, he became amazed. When we came out, his face was radiant beyond description.

order.why: Keep the later reported summary of speaking across religious settings.
shortened: So it was with us. We had not traveled before so when we started, we went on a long journey. Every day, we were in a town or a city. Indeed, the American cities are very large. I spoke of the validity of his holiness, Christ, and of the accepted Messenger (Mohammed) in most of the Christian churches and in the synagogues of the Jews.

order.why: Read the letter’s account of divine unity proclaimed in synagogues.
Preserve the narrated church visit and beginning of the Bible inscription.
Keep the hotel encounter’s changing welcome in its reported context.
Read the remembered Washington meetings and claim about reception as reported.
shortened: In Europe, in the great assemblies talks were given. I spoke to the eminent people.

Did you ever see in America, in Washington, in the Churches and meetings that anyone rose to oppose me? It was in your house in Washington that there was a general meeting in the morning and one for the notables on the afternoon.

order.why: Keep the reported appeal to inspiration when speaking.
Preserve the Chicago address’s assertion about the journey’s unusual character.
shortened: Look at the history of the world and try to find a parallel instance in which a native of the East has come to the countries of the West, particularly America, and called out to them in the churches and meetings there, raised the divine call in many of the large cities and invited everyone to the Abha Kingdom, with no one taking exception.

order.why: Keep the retrospective reported claim concerning the reception of the teachings.
shortened: Throughout many cities of America and Europe, in Churches and meetings with a loud voice I declared these Teachings and there was found not a single soul to contradict them."

order.why: Read the New York church invitation and onward plan for Montclair.
Keep the brief report of returning from Boston.
Read the reported self-questioning on entering a new city.
shortened: While I was travelling in America whenever I entered a new city I looked around and said it to myself: 'Why am I here? What relation exists between me and the United States? This is made possible through the Bestowals of the Blessed Perfection. During my stay in Boston I delivered an address at the annual Banquet of the Unitarian Association where more than 800 Ministers were present.

order.why: Explore the northeastern journey through seed and tree imagery.
Keep the specific account of visits to Chicago.
Read the reported discussion of an invitation to California.
Preserve the earlier regret concerning a California visit.
shortened: It was my hope to come to California and see the faces of the friends; but I regret that I am obliged to return to the Orient.

order.why: Follow the changed plan prompted by Californian invitations.
Keep the immediate journey to Kenosha beside the decision for California.
shortened: Despite this, it is midnight and I have risen from my bed to write this letter. In the morning I am bound for Kenosha, and I am determined to go to California.

order.why: Read the short San Francisco letter’s picture of intense activity.
Retain the concise reported statement of distance traveled.
shortened: I have come a long distance to see you; I have traveled 12,000 miles.

order.why: Keep the reported reminder to Seattle and Portland friends of time away.
shortened: It is now over menthe seven and a half months - that I have been here, and it is two years since I left the Holy Land, leaving all my concerns there to come here, as I longed to see the Friends of God.

order.why: Read the request to explain the needs of waiting Eastern pilgrims.
Reach the Pacific limit and the longing to return to the Shrine.
shortened: O how we miss you, O how we miss you!

In short, the journey has reached its end and the dawn of return has broken, for we have reached the shores of the Pacific Ocean. Beyond this are the Hawaiian Islands and the countries of China and Japan. The distance is great, strength and power have reached their limit. Now we must turn toward the Center of the Sun of Truth and hasten to the Holy Shrine, that I may lay my face upon its dust and make my hair fragrant and perfumed.

order.why: Preserve the reported comfort of the three-day journey toward Denver.
Keep the separate report of travel from California toward Chicago.
Read the cable’s practical uncertainty about sailing.
Keep the reported prospect of the journey’s later significance aboard the Celtic.
shortened: Then it becomes clear what importance this journey will acquire - that we raised the call of Ya Baha'u'l-Abha in the great churches and major assemblies, and with eloquent speech and perfect proof gave the glad-tidings of the Kingdom of God and explained the teachings of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Read the Vienna interview’s route summary as reported.
Give the obligation to keep a promise a place in travel planning.
shortened: But alas, the appointed time of arrival is the fourth of the month, while this yearning one will be departing for Paris on the morning of the third month, as some respected individuals have extended invitations and I have made promises, and breaking promises is wrong.

order.why: Attend to the detailed Edinburgh schedule and hoped-for onward travel.
Preserve the separate plan for Scotland and Paris with its omissions.
Keep the brief lack of time in crowded London.
Read the simple notice of writing in Paris.
Retain the separate concise Paris location.
Keep the cable’s minimal report of arrival.
Notice the unanswered letter read in a Paris morning.
Read the arrival in Paris through the renewed companionship of Amin and his son.
Keep the gratitude for a companion’s long journey to London and Paris.
Recounts the decision to leave Paris and urges continued work in London.
Let a personal longing explain the Paris and proposed Stuttgart visit.
shortened: This trip to Paris was just for your sake. I am longing very much to see you. God willing, I shall come to Stuttgart. However, I will not stay more than two nights and this is according to the requirement of wisdom.

order.why: Retain the hope of travel to Germany.
Keep the short retrospective reference to Hungary, Vienna and Germany.
Read the rapidly changing European itinerary with its source omission.
shortened: While in Europe one day we were in London and another in Edinburgh; now in Paris and anon in Stuttgart; once in Budapest and again in Vienna. We were almost every hour in one place, delivering lengthy speeches and addresses and notwithstanding the indisposition of the body day and night I cried and raised my voice in large meetings and important Churches...

order.why: Preserve the reported explanation of an unexpectedly long Paris stay.
shortened: I have been travelling for two and a half years. Nowhere was I ill except here, where due to illness I had to stay a long time. If I had not become ill, I would not have stayed in Paris more than a month.

order.why: Keep the reported discussion of therapeutic baths and invitations.
Read the remembered comparisons of favorable climates as recollection.
shortened: I traveled in many countries. I went to the world's most famous climates, such as Dublin, New Hampshire, the summer resort of Washington's government officials and statesmen.
Also, we went to Denver, Colorado.
Again, we were in Switzerland, which is far famed, and in the summer people from all regions go there.

order.why: Return to the letter’s sense of continual movement.
Keep the urgency of changing place morning and evening.
shortened: O scion of the blessed Tree! We are on a journey, we are in haste. Each morning we are in one country, each evening we are wanderers.

order.why: Let the express train connect distant gatherings.
Read the journey through the homeless-bird image.
Preserve the separate account of ceaseless travel and proclaiming the eastern Sun.
Keep the further image of a bird without shelter and the work of explanation.
Let the helpless bird’s call rise through the journey’s uncertainty.
shortened: Throughout this period of wandering and homelessness, the cry of this helpless bird reached the height of heaven, while the call of 'Ya Baha'u'l-Abha!' thrilled the ears of the world's people.

order.why: Read release from confinement through song and movement, retaining the omission.
Keep the letter’s own account of duration, illness and travels.
shortened: Although five years ago, due to severe hardships, my physical frame could not endure and various illnesses befell me, yet for four years 'Abdu'l-Baha wandered through mountains and deserts, lost in wilderness and seas, and throughout all the western countries gave the glad-tidings of the appearance of the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Retain the brief reference to the three illnesses and continuing movement.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha, while afflicted with three illnesses, suddenly left Haifa and has been continuously traveling for three years.

order.why: Read the decision to act before death in the letter’s own terms.
Keep the separate statement of leaving important responsibilities despite illness.
Preserve the letter’s retrospective account of a four-year undertaking.
Return to the message concerning war and peace.
Keep the appeal to people of insight and learning in the selected wording.
shortened: I renounced all peace, tranquility and rest in this Luminous Spot, and, notwithstanding my advanced age, left behind my kindred and traversed both land and sea, to lift up my voice in the vast assemblies and gatherings of both Europe and the Americas, and to address mankind from the depth of my being, calling aloud and saying:
'O ye men of insight! O ye exponents of learning!

order.why: Read the reported purpose of awakening spiritual attention.
shortened: My object in taking that long journey through the West- was to awaken them out of this sleep; that they may not grovel all the time in the world of matter and that they may not only think of eating and drinking.

order.why: Retain the letter’s claimed consequences and universal proclamation in its setting.
shortened: In this year, calamities and the blow of economic depression and corruption have encompassed all horizons, for the proof has been completed for all: 'Abdu'l-Baha, in churches and gatherings throughout Europe and America, in most great cities, proclaimed the Cause of Baha'u'llah with raised voice and called to the Abha Kingdom. He established brilliant proofs and manifested clear and evident demonstrations and conclusive arguments, leaving no excuse for anyone.

order.why: Keep the concise account of public proclamation.
Read unceasing activity as a hoped-for step in self-effacement.
shortened: I am in Europe and have no rest day or night, hoping that I may draw a breath in servitude at the Sacred Threshold and take a step on the path of self-effacement and nothingness.

order.why: Read the whole journey as sustained teaching.
shortened: Consider how 'Abdu'l-Baha forgot all thoughts and mentions and turned His face toward the countries and empires, cities and villages, mountains and deserts of the West. Day and night He was engaged in teaching the Cause and conveying the Message.

order.why: Preserve the specific account of less than a year in America.
shortened: Less than a year 'Abdu'l-Baha raised the cry of "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha" from his heart and soul as he crossed the mountains and deserts of that continent and in churches and meetings he imparted the glad-tidings of the appearance of the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Keep the separate portrayal of that American period.
shortened: Less than a year Abdul Baha traveled through the cities of America and crossed its deserts and from his heart and soul he raised the cry of Ya Baha El Abha; in gatherings and churches he gave the Glad-Tidings of the appearance of the Kingdom of God; vociferously he imparted the news of the dawn of the Sun of Reality; he explained divine Proofs and Evidences and with a spirit and mind overflowing with the Love of God He sung the New Melody.

order.why: Consider the letter’s emphasis on the capacity of the hearers.
Read the distinction drawn between European and American opportunities.
Turn the example toward the manner of future teaching.
shortened: Now the friends of God must adopt the manner and conduct of 'Abdu'l-Baha and strive day and night to teach the Cause of God, but in the way that 'Abdu'l-Baha did in America.

order.why: Preserve the reported musical analogy for beginning public speaking.
Read the reported preparation to speak when physical voice was weak.
shortened: 'Abdu'l-Baha stated,

When I went to America, My fatigue was of such a degree that My voice could not reach more than a few meters. Of necessity, in gatherings of four or five thousands souls, I would first concentrate on the Blessed Beauty and then begin speaking.

order.why: Keep the separate recollection of prayer before a long address.
shortened: When travelling in America and Europe, on many occasion[s] I did not have the power of uttering one word but before entering the meeting I begged Baha'u'llah to reinforce me and then walked in and commenced to speak for one or two hours.

order.why: Preserve the reported experience of spiritual confirmation in meetings.
shortened: When I entered a convention or a meeting I saw with my own eyes the confirmations of the Holy Spirit hovering like white-plumaged birds over my head and the Kingdom of existence with all its mighty forces coming to my assistance. All the days and nights were spent for the Cause and all the conversations and talks revolved around the Cause.

order.why: Keep the attribution of others’ attention to divine assistance.
shortened: Were it not for His confirmations, in the Western countries no one would have paid even the slightest attention to me.

order.why: Read the short reported acknowledgment of guided service.
Keep the reported image of visible solitude and unseen support.
shortened: This is why I abandoned every task, every thought, every mention, every imagination, and for three and a half years I went through deserts, mountains, valleys, cities and countries, raising my voice and crying out.

Like the sun in the second year after the Ascension, I wrote a letter to one of the friends which included this verse: "O Abbas, mounted alone, charge into the ranks of the world!" In brief, I went to those regions and saw that I was moving alone among their temples, gatherings, assemblies and churches, but I was supported by hosts that you cannot see.

order.why: Read the later recollection of arduous travel and confirmation.
Preserve the letter’s account of some relief after departure.
Keep the reported joy in remembering American service.
Let the concise personal remembrance of luminous days stand alone.
shortened: The days I spent with you were spiritual and luminous.

order.why: Attend to longing for Eastern friends during Western travel.
Read the remembered verse of Sadi alongside repeated city visits.
Keep the letter’s refusal of repeated requests for photographs.
shortened: In Paris and London, numerous journalists and newspaper people insisted greatly on taking photographs, but this servant did not consent.

order.why: Compare the reported difficulty of avoiding professional photographers.
Read the concern to avoid any appearance of seeking Mrs. Hearst’s money.
shortened: In my journey to America, I never spoke of her [Mrs. Hearst], and when others spoke of her, I maintained silence so that no one would think that we had an eye on her money. Upon arrival in California, Goodall and Cooper asked that I meet with her [Mrs. Hearst].

order.why: Keep the reported refusal of offered travel funds.
shortened: So far, very few people have lived according to this behest, but it is my will to live accordingly. Before coming to America, the believers of God, through Mirza Ahmad Sohrab, offered for my traveling expenses 16,000 dollars, but I did not accept one cent.

order.why: Preserve the letter’s qualifications about contributions and charitable expenses.
shortened: When friends in the West wished to make contributions, whether small or large, towards these expenses, they were absolutely refused.

Nevertheless, in view of an all-encompassing wisdom, we have kept this matter silent in the West, and if anyone wished to present something, we did not accept it, except in the beginning from one or two individuals for charitable expenses.

order.why: Read the detailed account of expenses and returned funds in its own wording.
shortened: As the journey to America lies ahead with an accompanying group and endless expenses - that is, costly - though the expenses were kept with utmost frugality as you observed in Alexandria. In Paris, in one day the cost reached six hundred liras, but the expenses for all of us, that is with companions, despite Paris being expensive, was half a lira, and so forth. From America they sent three thousand and some pounds for travel expenses, but it was not entirely accepted and was returned. The intention is that even hospitality should not be accepted, and in this there is complete wisdom.

order.why: Keep the historically specific request for discretion about whereabouts.
Consider the requested respite from letter writing.
Read the letter begun before departure and sent from crowded London.
Keep the general apology for unanswered correspondence.
Preserve the separate explanation of a delayed reply.
Connect intricate questions and public addresses with another delayed answer.
shortened: Due to bodily infirmity, the difficulties of traveling over seas and lands, lack of rest, striving and exerting day and night, delivering long addresses in different cities, and answering the varied, intricate questions of people, 'Abdu'l-Baha has not been able to answer it.

order.why: Read the daily schedule through its physical effects.
shortened: Due to the length of travel by sea and land, the great hardships day and night, lack of rest and sleep, and detailed addresses in public gatherings, physical weakness and exhaustion resulted. From sunrise until midnight in America there were either questions and answers or talks and addresses.

order.why: Keep the distinct fuller enumeration of the journey’s demands.
Follow travel from Montreal through sleeplessness and public work.
shortened: O thou my daughter in the Kingdom!

From the day of leaving Montreal until now I have not rested nor reposed for a moment. From morn until midnight I was engaged in heralding the Kingdom, and in numerous assemblages and meetings, even in the Jewish Temple, I raised the call proclaiming the Revelation of the Kingdom. Many a night I did not sleep, and on many a day, like unto a surging sea, I was in the utmost state of agitation.

order.why: Notice the night ending without even time to change clothes.
Keep the account of fatigue persisting after years of travel.
shortened: The reason was fatigue from travel and extreme exhaustion and physical ailments which still persist, for I was continuously traveling for four years without any rest. Anyone else in my place would have been completely worn down to skin and bones.

order.why: Read the stark image of exhausted limbs.
Preserve the report of physicians’ warnings in Paris.
Keep the letter’s detailed account of changing climates, cities and illness.
shortened: I stayed in these parts for several days, because from the length of travel and storms at sea and different climates of mountain and desert in America, and journeys in European lands - one day in London, another time in Paris, days in Germany, periods in Vienna, days in Bucharest, every hour in a different place - and continuously giving talks and addresses, despite poor health, engaged night and day in proclamation and outcry in great gatherings and grand churches, therefore this earthly frame could not withstand these endless hardships and became ill and weak.

order.why: Read the account of illness after returning eastward.
Retain the separate statement of sickness following the voyage.
shortened: After my return from America and Europe, owing to the difficulties of the long voyage and the innumerable inconveniences of the journey, a reaction set in and I became sick.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast with youthful capacity.
Read thanksgiving for some healing after danger.
Notice the cautious resumption of a short letter.
Preserve the reported account of returning to Egypt for rest while correspondence continues.
shortened: When I was in America I was most busy. Often I addressed three meetings in a day and gave innumerable interviews from early morning till midnight. In Europe I spread certain divine Teachings which will insure security to the human world and taught them that the foundation of the religions of God is one and the same. Now I have returned to Egypt in order to rest from the effect of this arduous journey and while I am here correspondence is uninterrupted [sic] with all parts of the West.

order.why: Keep the recollection of a promise to resume correspondence.
shortened: Before leaving for America I wrote to them that during my journey they must excuse me from any letter-writing, that after my return I will write to them as of old and now I am fulfilling my promise"
When we left I ventured to say that many petitions from America and Europe are accumulated that invite his attention.

order.why: Read the journey’s completion in Paris and turn toward the East.
Retain the separate notice of projected onward travel.
Keep the return from West to East in its scriptural geographical imagery.
shortened: After a period of travelling through mountain and desert, and voyaging over ocean and sea, I have returned from the West to the East, and have entered into the ancient land of Joseph the Canaanite.

order.why: Read the brief letter from Port Said.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! From my journey to America and Europe, I hastened toward Africa, and now in Port Said I have undertaken to write this letter.

order.why: Let arrival in Port Said bring relief in remembrance.
Keep the joyful repeated announcement of returning from Europe.
Direct return toward the two holy Shrines.
Read the renewed beginning of correspondence after three years.
Keep the meeting with Zoroastrian believers after returning East.
shortened: O ye kind friends! When I returned from the Western regions to the Eastern clime, I met the Zoroastrian Believers.

order.why: Preserve the reported account of returning to the Holy Land and its geographical descriptions.
Read the commitment to continued service after safe return.
Keep the request for another person to report the journey’s events.
Consider the reported lack of systematic documentation during the first journey.
shortened: During the first journey to Europe no one was thinking to do this work. Now and then Mirza Bager Khan, who was a member of our party, wrote down a few addresses and dates, but no systematic attempt was made in this direction.

order.why: Retain the original selection identifying Mabel McCoy Irwin’s account.
Read the narrated concern about misrepresenting the Educational Society’s standing.
Preserve the reported comparison of companions in its particular setting.
shortened: During this journey to America, certain souls showed humility and companionship, compared to whom people like Brown are not worth mentioning.

order.why: Keep the stated anticipation of results and opponents’ response.
Notice a personal awakening attributed to the call in Paris.
Read the letter’s report of activity following the Los Angeles visit.
Distinguish immediate impressions from effects not yet manifest.
shortened: Thou hast written regarding the results of my trip to America. Its importance is not now manifest. Ere long you shall behold that these pure seeds have grown and how adorned the green meadow and verdant rose-garden.

order.why: Keep the reported question about returning and the answer concerning harvests.
Read the later reported possibility of return through the image of a magnet.
Connect the prospect of another journey with harmony and lived teachings.
Keep the separate insistence on conditions that make a journey fruitful.
shortened: Therefore pray thou that harmony may be created so that your country may find the capacity for the Presence of Abdul-Baha. I have the utmost yearning to meet all of you; but unless the conditions which have been previously mentioned are realized, my trip to those parts would be difficult, for it would produce no results.

order.why: Retain the acknowledgment of anticipated joy and stated conditions.
shortened: O thou real beloved!

The letter which thou hast written in regard to the happiness and joy, beatitude and rejoicing of the American believers concerning the trip of Abdul-Baha to the country of Joseph of Canaan, and likewise their expectation of my going to America was perused. However, the latter event is depended upon several conditions which are already explained in a former Tablet.

order.why: Read the prepared places alongside the image of a fragrant breeze.
shortened: Regarding my coming to America, you wrote that the friends have prepared places for my arrival.
Whenever a fragrant breeze reaches Our nostrils, surely the journey will be undertaken.

order.why: Keep the flowers-and-thistles invitation and the reply about results.
shortened: Thou hast invited me to America saying that in that region and in that country there are many fragrant and multicolored flowers, likewise there are thorns and thistles but Abdul-Baha should not look upon the thistles of the desert.

I have the utmost longing to meet all of you but unless the conditions which have been previously mentioned are realized my trip to those parts would be difficult for it would not produce any results.

order.why: Let the prospect of a pleasant feast convey longing.
shortened: If such a delicious, sweet and pleasant feast is prepared and arranged, surely Abdul-Baha will fly to America to partake of that feast.

order.why: Preserve the renewed possibility linked to enkindlement.
Read the reported difficulty of another visit even if undertaken differently.
Keep the reported reply preferring nearer destinations.
Allow future travel to follow the completion of present service.
Remember the European response despite a lack of possessions and fame.
shortened: You observed what a great commotion arose in Europe.
However, 'Abdu'l-Baha, despite weakness and having no belongings or fame, entered those regions.

order.why: Join prayer with the image of racing steeds running together.
Keep the reported request for prayer for service in both East and West.
shortened: Will you ever return to America again?
Answer by Abdul Baha:

It is in God's hands. Pray for me to return and say: "O Baha'u'llah! Confirm Abdul Baha in the Cause of God. Confirm him in the servitude of God in the East, so that he may not spend all of his time in the Orient, that he may return to America and occupy his time in the Western world."

order.why: Pass the call to travel and serve to another person.
shortened: Now is the time that thou mayst go to America and exert in the promotion of the Cause of God and the exaltation of the Word of God and [self-sacrifice] in the Path of God."

order.why: Read the reported intention to prepare others to carry the work after departure.
shortened: While in America I strove day and night to prepare a few, holy sanctified souls to take up the burden of the Cause after my departure.

order.why: Let the finitude of life sharpen the purpose of service.
Close with the reported long journey and hoped-for rest, preserving its source context.
shortened: As to the second point--I am going to take a long journey and at that time my spirit will rest."

questions: Which small details bring the journeys closest to your experience, and how do they change your understanding of their larger purpose?
How do letters, public addresses, narrated encounters, and later recollections offer different kinds of evidence about the same undertaking?
What relationships among love, courage, bodily limitation, prayer, and companionship emerge from the accounts of travel?
How do encounters across religions and cultures connect the journey’s manner with its message about human unity?
What similarities and differences do you notice between Luke’s traveling messengers and these accounts, especially concerning hospitality, support, and bringing peace?
How might the significance of a visit continue to unfold after the traveler leaves, and what would the connected subject on growth help you investigate?

references.label: 1 · Luke 10:1–9 · Carrying peace from place to place
references.note: Jesus sends messengers in pairs, connects their work with a harvest, and instructs them to bring peace into the homes that receive them. Compare this mission’s hospitality and dependence on hosts with the particular arrangements described in the journeys here. What makes travel an act of service, and how can its form vary with its purpose and circumstances?
